stages.name: Orblet
stages.bio: Orblet is a tiny round creature with one enormous violet eye that fills most of its body. Four stubby fins keep it bobbing just off the seafloor while its soft purple skin pulses faintly with each thought. In Coral Bay's shallows it floats between the reef columns, fixing that giant unblinking eye on anything that moves - not to hunt, but out of pure bottomless curiosity. Guardians say Orblet memorizes the shape of every fish it meets, storing them somewhere in the inky depths of its mind.
stages.note: Orblet never blinks - researchers believe it photographs a full scene with each long stare.

stages.name: Sharkmaw
stages.bio: Sharkmaw has grown a streamlined blue-and-purple shark body, long pointed snout, and swept-back purple fins edged in lilac. Its massive single eye now glows with a sharper violet light, and a ridge of psychic energy runs along its dorsal line. It patrols the mid-water columns of Coral Bay with calm precision, reading the intentions of creatures before they even move. Trainers who respect its gaze find it an eerily reliable early-warning partner when Abalont's shadows creep near the reef.
stages.note: Sharkmaw can feel a lie in the water before a single word is spoken - its eye turns deep indigo when it senses deception.

stages.name: Voidtide
stages.bio: Voidtide has transformed into a vast deep-blue manta ray whose wide flat wings are spotted with glowing pale-blue orbs. Trailing luminous tendrils drift behind it like living starlight. Its body measures wider than a rowboat and its passage creates a visible current. It no longer merely watches - it broadcasts its thoughts outward in waves that the reef's fish respond to by clearing a path. Ancient Coral Bay lore says Voidtide's mind-current once guided lost guardian ships home through pitch-black water.
stages.note: Every glowing spot on Voidtide's wings is a memory of a different voice it once heard; the oldest spots shine brightest.

stages.name: Seedling
stages.bio: A walking acorn no taller than a boot, Seedling wears a glossy ribbed cap pulled low over two big eyes, and swings a pair of little pinecone fists it loves to knock together when excited. Two green leaves sprout from its cap - they perk up at a brave new sound and droop when it grows sleepy. It was the first friend the guardians ever made in Verdant Valley, and it stayed among the roots when Akilla fell to Abalont's shadow.
stages.note: A tap-tap-tap through the undergrowth is usually a Seedling drumming its pinecone fists, calling for a friend.

stages.name: Oakmite
stages.bio: Standing upright now, Oakmite's body has hardened into ridged bark, and the leaves on its cap have grown into full sprigs that fan open in sunlight. Its pinecone fists have toughened into knotted knuckles it plants on the ground to brace itself - once set, it holds its place like a young tree in a storm. It patrols the climbing paths where Akilla once roamed.
stages.note: Oakmite refuses to step backward; trainers say you can move a boulder more easily than a planted Oakmite.

stages.name: Giantern
stages.bio: Broad and tree-solid, Giantern carries two great pinecone pods on its shoulders like a warrior's pauldrons, and its acorn-cap crown is thick as oak-heartwood. When it speaks, its voice rolls out as a deep groan of creaking wood, and the roots beneath the valley stir in answer. Patient as the forest itself, it remembers every voice and waits for the lost guardians to come home.
stages.note: The pods on its shoulders drop ripe seeds each autumn; a single one can grow into a new grove of song-trees.

name: Fluttox

stages.name: Fluttox
stages.bio: Fluttox is a plump sky-blue bird fledgling with soft round feathers and a single small iridescent crystal wing-fan sprouting beside its regular wing. Its eyes are wide and brilliantly blue, and it flaps both wings with cheerful uncoordinated enthusiasm. High in Gale Ridge's updraft chimneys, Fluttox tumbles on the wind currents, each tumble teaching it a little more about how air moves. Guardians of the Ridge leave seed perches on the upper platforms, knowing a tumbling Fluttox always finds its way back up.
stages.note: Fluttox somersaults exactly three times before landing - never two, never four, always three.

stages.name: Windox
stages.bio: Windox has grown into a proud blue-and-white bird with layered feathers and large iridescent crystal wings that catch every draft like sails. Its posture is alert and bold, chest forward, tail fanned wide. It rides the constant gales around Gale Ridge without flapping - just tilts a crystal feather and the wind does the rest. Windox scouts ahead of storms, calling back weather-reads to trainers below in a series of precise whistled patterns.
stages.note: Each whistled call from Windox encodes the wind direction, speed, and whether rain is coming - thirty notes, all distinct.

stages.name: Crystalwing
stages.bio: Crystalwing is a magnificent sea-green-and-teal eagle with enormous crystal-shard wings that catch the light like a stained-glass window mid-storm. Its wingspan blots out the sun when it passes overhead, and each crystal primary feather chimes against the others in a continuous moving melody. Its psychic perception now spans the full height of Gale Ridge - it reads thoughts the way a sailor reads clouds. Legends say Crystalwing once guided the guardians through Abalont's blindness-fog by broadcasting a psychic beacon from the tallest spire.
stages.note: When Crystalwing circles three times over the same spot, a storm will arrive within the hour - the Ridge's guardians trust this completely.

blurb: Fluttox got blown away from its flock by a big gust. Help Fluttox fly home!
watch: Watched over by the Guardian Jack.
facts: Birds are the only animals with feathers.
Parrots can copy sounds and even words!
question: What covers a bird's body?

stages.name: Amethib
stages.bio: Amethib is a small bright-green lizard with a yellow underbelly and a single large purple amethyst horn jutting from its forehead. Its scales are smooth and vibrant, and its long tail curves behind it with a jaunty flick. In Shadow Caves' dim passages it uses its horn to scratch glowing grooves into the cave walls - these marks are actually directions back to safe ground, a habit it has never stopped. Hatchling Amehibs emerge from the cave rock itself, as if the stone decided to grow legs.
stages.note: The scratch-marks Amethib leaves on cave walls form a complete map of its territory - readable to other Amehibs but not to outsiders.

stages.name: Amethrock
stages.bio: Amethrock has grown dramatically - now a hefty dark green and purple chameleon with a ridged dorsal fin of spiky crystal crests running from neck to tail. Its curling tail is thick and strong, and its wide-set eyes swivel independently. It can shift its color between deep green and murky purple to vanish into the shadow cave walls. The crystal crests secrete a faint toxic residue that smells of wet stone; creatures that touch them directly feel their thoughts scramble briefly.
stages.note: Amethrock can freeze mid-step for up to forty minutes, perfectly mimicking a jagged stalactite - even experienced cave-walkers step past it.

stages.name: Amethyx
stages.bio: Amethyx stands as an imposing upright lizard-beast, its body covered in overlapping armored scales of deep green and dark stone-grey. A towering crown of thick amethyst crystals erupts from its head like a jagged throne, and its broad chest gleams with iridescent gem-shards embedded in the skin. Its heavy clawed hands could crush boulders. Deep in Shadow Caves, Amethyx is the unquestioned keeper of the darkest passages - other cave creatures step aside, and the shadows themselves seem to bow.
stages.note: The crystal crown on Amethyx's head absorbs toxic vapors and converts them into stored energy - it grows larger the deeper in the cave it lives.

stages.name: Anchorpup
stages.bio: Anchorpup is a stocky dark-grey crab with a rounded shell etched with anchor symbols and bright orange hair-like frills sprouting from its head and claws like a rocky sea-creature's crown. Two small anchor-engraved shields sit embedded in its shell. It scuttles sideways along the granite coastlines where Granite Heights meets the sea, wedging itself into rock crevices when the tide comes in. Young Anchorpups anchor themselves so firmly that fishermen have been known to mistake them for actual fixed harbor hardware.
stages.note: Anchorpup can lock its legs into a rock crack so tightly that twenty children pulling together cannot move it.

stages.name: Anchoreel
stages.bio: Anchoreel has grown into an imposing dark slate-blue crab with a massive ridged shell and three large decorative anchor-shields embedded across its back and claws. Its orange crest-frills have thickened into dense tufts around its eyes and flanks, giving it a wild salt-spray look. Its claws can grip ocean boulders bare enough to strip barnacles in one pull. In Granite Heights' tidal pools it acts as an anchor for smaller creatures during storms - they cling to its shell as it braces against currents that would sweep them away.
stages.note: In a gale, up to forty smaller creatures have been counted sheltering on a single Anchoreel's shell - it never seems to notice the weight.

stages.name: Colossamchor
stages.bio: Colossamchor is a fortress of a crab - massive dark stone body with a shell as thick as harbor walls, orange coral-frills cascading from its head and flanks, and enormous anchor emblems carved deep into its two front shields. Its claws could redirect a river. It stands at the granite cliffs where the great ocean meets the Heights, and the tide literally rises and falls a few centimeters differently when it shifts position. Ancient mariners built their first harbor walls by tracing the curve of a sleeping Colossamchor.
stages.note: The tidal rhythm at Granite Heights Cove has matched Colossamchor's breathing pattern for three hundred recorded years.

stages.name: Chirplet
stages.bio: Chirplet is a small plump golden-yellow fledgling with rounded wing-stubs, a short beak, and wide dark eyes that gleam with intelligence above its oversized round head. Its fluffy yellow breast feathers trap wind and make it bounce slightly even on calm days. In Gale Ridge's lower cliff pockets it sits facing the prevailing wind with its beak open - not eating, but tasting the air, learning each note of the storm's voice. Chirplet's own song is a single pure note, held as long as its small lungs allow.
stages.note: Chirplet holds a single sung note for up to forty-five seconds without breathing - Gale Ridge musicians use it to tune their instruments.

stages.name: Goldwing
stages.bio: Goldwing has grown into a robust upright golden bird with a bright orange-yellow breast, neat compact wings, and a clarion singing voice that carries clear across Gale Ridge's upper platforms. It opens its beak wide when singing, projecting with surprising force for its size. It rides the thermal columns around the Ridge in long lazy spirals, releasing song-phrases that the wind carries and reshapes into new melodies a kilometer away. Gale Ridge guardians used Goldwing song-patterns as long-distance message codes.
stages.note: Goldwing's song changes rhythm depending on wind speed - researchers have mapped twenty distinct patterns, each encoding a different weather condition.

stages.name: Solstryx
stages.bio: Solstryx has expanded into a broad-winged golden raptor with wide spread wings that catch every sun-ray and convert it to lift. Its golden-amber plumage blazes in full light, and its open-winged display shows stripes of deeper bronze beneath. It soars the highest thermal arches above Gale Ridge without a single wingbeat for hours at a time. Its song is no longer a single note but a full harmonic chord - sung on the exhale into the storm's core and heard by creatures fifty kilometers in every direction.
stages.note: Solstryx soars for an average of six hours between wingbeats; the longest recorded continuous glide is eleven hours and forty minutes.

stages.name: Aurkit
stages.bio: Aurkit is a vivid green kitten with bright yellow-green spots scattered across its round body, a plump curved tail, and wide innocent teal eyes. Its soft jungle-green fur smells faintly of fresh leaves after rain. In Shadow Caves it is an unlikely inhabitant - it wanders in from the forest edge and seems genuinely unbothered by the dark, since its spots faintly glow in the absence of light. Young trainers find it irresistible, and Aurkit returns the affection by bumping its head against anyone who crouches down to its level.
stages.note: Aurkit's spots glow brighter when it learns a name it has never heard - a particularly bright flash means it understood something important.

stages.name: Aurfang
stages.bio: Aurfang has grown into a lithe and powerful green-and-gold leopard with large sunflower-pattern spots and bright sharp teal eyes that pierce the cave dark. Its muscles move smoothly under its sleek coat, and its claws click lightly on the cave floor. In Shadow Caves it has found its purpose - patrolling the boundary between the forest and the dark, guiding lost creatures back to the light. It carries the scent of jungle flowers into the deepest shadows, which is strangely comforting to creatures trapped in the dark.
stages.note: Aurfang's scent-trail through Shadow Caves leads outward, never inward - any creature that follows its smell finds the forest edge within ten minutes.

stages.name: Aurmawlix
stages.bio: Aurmawlix is a magnificent large jungle cat with emerald-and-gold spotted fur, powerful wide forequarters, and a dramatic pair of lush green leaf-wings unfurling from its shoulders like a forest canopy taking flight. Its mane is a rich tangle of deep green vines and glowing teal markings trace the lines of its face and sides. In Shadow Caves it stands as a living bridge between darkness and light - its wings carry the scent of the deep forest into places where the forest has never been, and creatures come out of the shadows to follow it home.
stages.note: When Aurmawlix opens its wings fully in Shadow Caves, photosynthesis occurs in the immediate vicinity - moss blooms on cave walls within minutes.

name: Azukit

stages.name: Azukit
stages.bio: Azukit is a small blue-furred kitten dusted with darker blue spots and carrying a thin water-dripping tail that leaves wet paw-sized puddles wherever it wanders. Its wide eyes hold a distant look - not lost, but listening to something just below hearing. Azukit paws at the tide pools of Coral Bay for hours, not hunting but reading, as though each ripple carries a message. The guardians' diaries describe a small blue kit that sat at the water's edge and whispered the next day's weather to anyone who leaned in close enough.
stages.note: Azukit whispers the next day's wave height into the ears of sleeping tide-pool crabs - the crabs are always right.

stages.name: Azumaul
stages.bio: Azumaul stands taller now, its blue fur patterned with flowing wave-curl markings that shift like liquid in sunlight. Its slender curling tail drips constantly - not with weakness but with surplus - the water it carries seems to refill from somewhere unseen. Azumaul walks the reef's edge at high tide, occasionally pressing a paw to the surface and watching where the ripple travels, charting currents that would take a ship's navigator an hour to calculate. It has a habit of arriving precisely when it is needed and leaving before anyone can thank it.
stages.note: Azumaul's paw-print in wet sand can last through a full tide cycle without washing away - fishers mark it as lucky.

stages.name: Azuravox
stages.bio: Azuravox has grown into a broad-chested deep-blue lion whose entire body is mapped in scale-like wave patterns that ripple as it breathes. Its long flowing water-tail moves with the cadence of a slow ocean current, never still. When it speaks - a sound between a roar and a cresting wave - the sea answers with a swell that rocks every boat in Coral Bay. Ancient records say Azuravox once pushed back a tide that Abalont had drawn away to strand the guardians, holding the sea back with its body for three days until help arrived.
stages.note: Azuravox breathes in time with the tides - twice per day - and the coral reefs bloom visibly at each exhale.

blurb: Azukit got separated from its pack by the tide. Help Azukit get back to them!
watch: Watched over by the Guardian Axon.
facts: A cat's whiskers help it feel things around it.
Cats can see well in the dark.
question: What helps a cat feel things?

stages.name: Scaldrak
stages.bio: Scaldrak is a stocky blue-scaled lizard whose back is lined with a vivid row of red and orange spines that glow with internal heat. It scrambles across the Lava Crater's cooled rock shelves with remarkable grip, using its broad claws to anchor against sudden steam vents. The spines puff up double when it is startled, making it look twice as fierce as it is. Scaldrak has a habit of licking the warm stones to taste where the heat is strongest, marking good basking spots with a single claw-scratch so it can find them again.
stages.note: Blazlet scratches a single claw-mark on each new basking stone to remember it - the crater walls are covered in its tiny record-keeping.

stages.name: Blazorn
stages.bio: Blazorn stands upright now, tall and barrel-chested, its blue scales hardened to near-ceramic and the red-orange spines along its back grown into a bold ridge that radiates heat visibly. A pair of forward-curving horn-like spines crown its head and it uses them to push through cooled lava flows that would stop most creatures cold. Blazorn is territorial about the Lava Crater's best thermal vents, and its deep guttural warning call rattles loose rocks from the crater walls. Young ones come to it to be warmed during the crater's rare cold nights.
stages.note: Blazorn's back-ridge radiates enough heat to soft-boil a stone egg in thirty minutes - crater birds use its sleeping body as a nest warmer.

stages.name: Infernazard
stages.bio: Infernazard is a mountain of scaled muscle and fire, its blue-armored body crowned with enormous bat-like wings that turn the air above the crater into a shimmering heat column when spread. The full ridge of blazing red-orange spines along its back glows like an open forge, and its tail sweeps cooled lava into spray with casual swings. Ancient guardians named it the Crater's Lock - as long as Infernazard nests at the Lava Crater's heart, the volcano's pressure holds steady, and Abalont's shadow cannot take root in the magma below.
stages.note: Infernazard's wing-spread over the crater creates a thermal column so strong that ash from the last eruption can still be found in orbit.

stages.name: Blazkit
stages.bio: Blazkit is a small blue armadillo with a rounded shell and a tuft of yellow spines along its back that stick out like a crown it hasn't grown into yet. It trundles across the Granite Heights with a rolling gait, tapping the rock with its blunt snout to listen for hollow spaces beneath. When it finds one, it marks the spot with a drool-print - an indispensable skill that the heights' miners quietly rely on. Blazkit rolls into a tight ball when startled but immediately unrolls to check if the danger was interesting enough to deserve a better look.
stages.note: Blazkit's snout-tap can locate a hollow rock cavity down to three meters - the Heights' miners follow its trail before drilling.

stages.name: Blazorm
stages.bio: Blazorm's shell has thickened into a heavy ridged dome the color of polished granite, and its yellow crest-spines have grown broad and flat like shields. It walks with its head low, powerful arms swinging, and can overturn a two-meter boulder without breaking its stride. The Granite Heights' communities know Blazorm by the perfectly smooth bowl-shaped depressions it leaves when it rests - pressed into solid rock. It does not sleep lightly; once it settles, not even a thunderstorm will wake it before it is ready.
stages.note: Blazorm's resting-bowl impressions in granite are smooth as polished marble - climbers use them as handholds on the sheer heights.

stages.name: Terrablazer
stages.bio: Terrablazer has grown so large and heavy that it no longer bothers walking overland - it bulldozes directly through the Granite Heights' stone, tunneling with the slow unstoppable force of a glacier. Its massive shell is now boulder-grey and its wide yellow spines flatten into plates as it plows forward. The Heights' surface is mapped in part by Terrablazer's tunnel network; whole communities have built over its passages without knowing. It surfaces once each season to check the sky, then disappears again, leaving a crater-like depression behind.
stages.note: Terrablazer's seasonal surfacing craters are precise enough that the Granite Heights' farmers use them as irrigation channels.

stages.name: Budscale
stages.bio: Budscale is a pale cream-and-green lizard with a vivid row of flower-petal-like spines cresting its back in blue, green, and yellow - a startling bloom of color on an otherwise quiet creature. It prowls the cooled lava margins of the crater where green things first push through cracked stone, eating the tender sprouts before they fully open. Budscale is remarkably hard to spot on volcanic rock until it flares its spine-crest in alarm, at which point it becomes impossible to miss. Young ones in a clutch always flare in sequence, creating a traveling wave of color along the whole group.
stages.note: When a group of Budscale flare their crests in sequence, the wave travels at exactly the speed of a walking human - no one knows why.

stages.name: Florasaur
stages.bio: Florasaur has grown upright and angular, its spine-crest now a full ridge of sharp purple and green thorns that extend and vibrate when it roars. The pale scales have deepened to a mottled green-yellow, and it moves with the sudden-start pace of a creature that is very still and then very fast. Florasaur claims a stretch of the Lava Crater's green margin as its territory, enforcing it with a spine-flash and a sharp hiss that most creatures respect without further negotiation. It is fond of rearranging its territory's rocks into rough rings - no one has determined why.
stages.note: Florasaur's rock rings are perfectly round within a centimeter - crater geologists have been quietly measuring them for years.

stages.name: Thorndrake
stages.bio: Thorndrake is a towering dark-scaled dragon whose enormous purple spike-mane rises from head to mid-back like a fortress palisade. The pale colouring is entirely gone - it has become all shadow-green and black with deep purple thorns that flex and clack when it breathes. Thorndrake is the Lava Crater's most unlikely guardian: a creature born of growing things that chose to root itself in fire, covering the green margins against Abalont's shadow by growing too fierce to be approached. It is said that where Thorndrake holds its ground, the first flowers through the lava never stop blooming.
stages.note: The patch of green below Thorndrake's regular resting spot is the most fertile ground in the entire Lava Crater - nothing there has ever died.

stages.name: Pigmote
stages.bio: Pigmote is a round brown boar-pup with a broad flat snout it uses to bulldoze through Sand Dune hillocks like a miniature plow. Rows of flat armored plates have already begun forming across its back, and two small rounded tusks poke out from a perpetually grumpy expression. It is surprisingly fast for its shape, and covers a lot of ground each day in a zigzag pattern as it roots for buried seeds and stone beetles. Pigmote does not share its food and will sit on anything edible it hasn't finished yet to stop others from reaching it.
stages.note: Pigmote sits on its unfinished food to save it for later - the dunes are dotted with its small flat depressions.

stages.name: Tuskling
stages.bio: Tuskling's back is now fully covered in overlapping stone-colored armor plates that clatter faintly as it moves, and its tusks have lengthened into forward-curving weapons that leave clean arcs in the dune sand when it charges. It tests every new piece of ground by stamping once before committing its full weight - a habit that has saved it from hidden sinkhole traps on dozens of occasions. Tuskling does not back down, but it is patient about choosing when to go forward, studying obstacles with small piggy eyes until it has a clear plan.
stages.note: Tuskling stamps once on every new surface before crossing - no Tuskling has ever fallen through a sand sinkhole.

stages.name: Boarthon
stages.bio: Boarthon is a walking stone fortress on four tree-trunk legs, its entire back covered in a fused shell of spiked rock plates and its tusks grown into great sweeping weapons that can carve a channel through a dune in a single pass. The ground shakes in rings when it walks, and approaching sand dunes visibly shift as the compression wave moves ahead of it. Boarthon is the Sand Dunes' unmovable anchor - when Abalont's shadow rolled across the dunes, Boarthon simply stood still in its path and did not move for nine days until the shadow went around it.
stages.note: Boarthon has stood completely still in the same spot for recorded periods of up to nine days - the dune shifts around it, not through it.

stages.name: Brahling
stages.bio: Brahling is a bright green caterpillar whose most striking feature is the glowing blue gem set into its forehead like a third eye that it cannot yet fully control. It blinks with all three eyes at different rates, creating a rhythm that the Crystal Mines' other creatures seem to find oddly calming. Brahling inches along the crystal veins in the mine walls, pressing its forehead gem against each crystal to listen - the gem briefly amplifies the crystal's natural hum to something audible. It is extraordinarily patient and will wait motionless for an hour for the right vibration.
stages.note: Brahling's forehead gem glows brighter near high-grade crystal deposits - miners call it the living dowsing rod.

stages.name: Brahman
stages.bio: Brahman has transformed completely - from crawling green larva to a tall graceful deer whose hide shimmers in green-and-gold crystal patterns and whose antlers are formed entirely of glowing crystal branches. It moves through the Crystal Mines with soundless delicacy, its hooves barely ringing on the stone, and tilts its antlered head to catch the light refracting from the walls. Brahman can broadcast the mines' crystal-hum as a visible light, briefly illuminating entire caverns when it raises its head. The mine workers leave gifts of polished crystals at its trail crossing.
stages.note: Brahman's antlers broadcast the mines' crystal-hum as light when raised - the deepest shafts have never needed lanterns where it walks.

stages.name: Divyahm
stages.bio: Divyahm is a magnificent towering stag whose full crown of golden crystal antlers reaches the ceiling of all but the Crystal Mines' grandest chambers, blazing with a warm amber-gold light that fills every crack and shadow in a hundred-meter radius. Gem-bright markings run from snout to tail in perfect symmetry, and when it breathes out, its breath carries a visible shimmer that settles into the mine walls as an iridescent residue. The guardians' oldest texts speak of Divyahm as the Mines' Memory - a creature who recorded every promise made in the crystal walls so nothing would be forgotten even if Abalont came.
stages.note: The iridescent residue of Divyahm's breath on crystal walls holds a clear impression of every voice raised near it for the past century.

stages.name: Bubkin
stages.bio: Bubkin is a round, small, purple creature with stubby fins and a large glowing pink bubble on top of its head that bobs when it moves, as though independently alive. It inhabits the Shadow Caves' quieter pools and tunnels, moving in a gentle slow-drift that belies how quickly it can vanish into the dark when startled. The bubble on its head pulses with a faint psychic light that other shadow-cave creatures find oddly soothing - Bubkin seems to produce it involuntarily as a by-product of thinking hard. It thinks very hard, very often.
stages.note: Bubkin's head-bubble pulses in time with its thoughts - the faster it pulses, the harder it's concentrating on something only it can see.

stages.name: Toadburst
stages.bio: Toadburst has expanded considerably - a wide, bumpy purple toad with several smaller glowing pink bubble-growths covering its back that pop and reform throughout the day. Each pop releases a brief psychic shimmer visible in the dark caves, and a faint sweet-and-wrong smell that is technically toxic but at cave-toad concentrations only produces an unusual sense of déjà vu. Toadburst sits in the same spot for days at a time, watching the cave's drip-patterns with absolute focus. The shadow creatures of the cave have learned to let it be - disturbing it mid-observation produces a triple-pop that leaves everyone confused about what day it is.
stages.note: Disturbing Toadburst mid-observation produces a triple-bubble-pop that causes a brief psychic disorientation lasting roughly one minute.

stages.name: Toxotaur
stages.bio: Toxotaur fills a cave chamber the way a thundercloud fills a sky - its massive broad body covered in large luminous pink bubble-nodules that glow and pulse with a rhythm that seems to sync with the heartbeat of anyone in the room. The psychic shimmer it broadcasts is now strong enough to cast visible shadows behind objects. In Ghost Hollow lore it is called the Dream-Lock: a creature that traps Abalont's shadow-agents in looping visions of words they never learned, keeping them confused and harmless in the deepest cave passages until the guardians can deal with them.
stages.note: Anything that enters Toxotaur's glow-radius without specific intent will spend the next hour convinced it has forgotten a very important word.

stages.name: Bublet
stages.bio: Bublet is an icy-blue pufferfish with a permanently disgruntled expression that it earned the day it was born and has maintained ever since. Its smooth round body is lightly textured like dimpled sea-glass and its small mouth is set in a downward curve of complete skepticism about everything. Bublet inhabits the cold-current channels of Frozen Peaks, where the icy upwellings keep the water clear and brisk. It has a habit of puffing up slightly - not full, just enough to communicate displeasure - whenever anything passes too close to the particular patch of current it has decided is its.
stages.note: Bublet's territory consists of exactly one cold-current patch two meters wide - it has never expanded it or abandoned it.

stages.name: Buboink
stages.bio: Buboink has grown a proper set of short, sharp spines across its body that it deploys in a ring when threatened, each one carrying a thin coating of ice that freezes anything pressing against it. Its expression has not improved with size - if anything, the larger face provides more surface area for displeasure. Buboink guards the cold-channel entrances of Frozen Peaks with the humorless efficiency of a toll collector who has never once been surprised to find someone trying to sneak past. It inflates to full size at the first sign of any trespass and holds it until the trespasser has been gone for at least five minutes.
stages.note: Buboink remains fully inflated for exactly five minutes after a trespasser leaves its territory - it has been measured repeatedly.

stages.name: Behemoth
stages.bio: Behemoth is an enormous ancient pufferfish whose spines have grown into long crystalline ice-lances covering every surface, and whose fully-inflated form is wide enough to plug a glacial outflow entirely. It is deeply grumpy in the way that only very old things that have watched everything go wrong for a very long time can be. Behemoth holds station in the deepest meltwater trench under Frozen Peaks, and the whole range's temperature stays stable as long as it rests there. The peaks-folk say the day Behemoth leaves its trench the thaw begins - and they are probably right.
stages.note: Behemoth has occupied the same meltwater trench for so long that the lakebed has permanently depressed around it by two meters.

stages.name: Sproutoad
stages.bio: Sproutoad is a round little toad the colour of wet soil, with a single white-budded sprout growing from between its eyes like a tiny candle. Its wide eyes blink slowly, and it sits almost perfectly still, watching. The sprout bobs when Sproutoad is excited and folds flat when it senses something creeping in the cave dark. Explorers in Shadow Caves use its flickering bud as a dim lantern, tiptoeing behind it through the blackest passages.
stages.note: The bud on Sproutoad's head glows faintly for about three seconds whenever it hears a name it has never heard it recognises.

stages.name: Thornogre
stages.bio: Thornogre has grown into something half-toad, half-thicket - its warty green hide is draped in rough leaf-layers, and a wild crown of thorned vines spirals from its head. A curling vine-tail trails behind it as it lumbers through the cave undergrowth. Its mouth stretches almost ear-to-ear, and it uses its long tongue not just to catch prey but to taste the air for the bitter scent of dark-energy surges. Shadow Caves explorers call it the gatekeeper of the deep passages.
stages.note: Thornogre never loses its way in the caves - it reads the dark with its tongue the way others read signs with their eyes.

stages.name: Verdewrath
stages.bio: Verdewrath is vast and low-slung, its body half-buried in its own wild moss and dark-vine growth. Glowing green vapour seeps from the dense tangle on its back, and its enormous flat head is nearly obscured by the living canopy it carries. It does not hunt - it simply opens its cavernous mouth and waits, patient as the cave itself, for the dark to bring things to it. Old tales say Verdewrath once swallowed a whole shadow-curse and slept for a century while the caves slowly brightened around it.
stages.note: The green vapour rising from Verdewrath's back is mildly sleep-inducing - visitors often wake up somewhere safer than where they started.

stages.name: Burmite
stages.bio: Burmite is a small, perfectly round green toad with a single leaf-bud antenna bouncing from its head. It has wide shiny eyes and a calm, settled posture - it sits on the warm sand of the dunes like a little green stone with opinions. The antenna flickers up in dry heat, drawing a tiny drop of moisture from the air. Dune travellers say stumbling on a Burmite means there is groundwater close beneath your feet.
stages.note: Burmite's antenna can sense underground moisture up to two metres down - desert guides treat it like a living well-finder.

stages.name: Burmoth
stages.bio: Burmoth has grown wide and solid, its smooth green hide now speckled with sandy earth tones. Three white-tipped antennae crown its head, bobbing in the desert breeze, and its sturdy legs end in broad flat pads that let it walk on loose sand without sinking. It digs shallow burrows each night and fills them with dew collected on its antennae. The blooms it leaves behind mark safe overnight stops for those who travel the Sand Dunes.
stages.note: Each Burmoth fills three small burrows with dew-water overnight - small desert creatures follow it like a moving oasis.

stages.name: Burmatog
stages.bio: Burmatog is a wide, heavy toad whose entire back has become a living garden of green spines and pale bloom-pods that release a faint sweet pollen on the desert wind. Its broad flat body presses close to the earth, and each slow step sends a vibration through the sand that is felt twenty paces away. When it calls at dusk, every plant within earshot unfurls a bloom in answer - as though the desert is responding to a word it has been waiting a very long time to hear.
stages.note: Burmatog calls at dusk every day without fail; botanists have confirmed the sand-bloom cycle follows its cry to the minute.

stages.name: Shellcrab
stages.bio: Shellcrab is a cheerful orange crab with a large translucent blue bubble-dome for a shell, through which its tiny face peers out with round bright eyes and a permanent grin. Its two front claws are bright orange and held wide in a gesture that could mean hello or challenge - often both at once. It skitters sideways across Coral Bay's tidal shallows, collecting small shiny objects and depositing them in its bubble-shell as though decorating a room. No two Shellcrab shells contain the same collection.
stages.note: Shellcrab collects exactly seven small objects before stopping for the day - if one is taken, it will search until the set is complete again.

stages.name: Ironpinch
stages.bio: Ironpinch is a formidable blue-grey crab with a heavily plated carapace studded with short spines and two large, asymmetric claws - the right distinctly bigger than the left, built for gripping, the left sharper for cutting. It moves quickly across the sea floor with a confident side-step and claims the largest tide pools in Coral Bay through sheer presence. Smaller creatures do not attempt to challenge it; they simply wait until it finishes eating and leave it whatever it did not take.
stages.note: Ironpinch always places its larger claw on the ground first when claiming a tide pool - marine biologists have confirmed it is a deliberate territorial signal, not accident.

stages.name: Titanomaw
stages.bio: Titanomaw is enormous and angular - its steel-blue carapace is plated in massive ridged sections, its claws broad and spiked, and its orange-rimmed eyes hold an intelligence that suggests it has outlasted several generations of everything around it. It moves with deliberate slowness in shallow water but is remarkably fast in the deep; Coral Bay fishers say if Titanomaw is hunting, the safest place is directly behind it. Its claws can cut through stone, but it reserves that capability - it has never been observed using it carelessly.
stages.note: Titanomaw has been documented at the same underwater rock formation every winter for at least forty recorded years - it is believed to be the same individual each time.

stages.name: Chitling
stages.bio: Chitling is a pale, chubby insect larva - smooth white skin banded in faint rings, a rounded rear, and a dark head with two tiny black eyes and a small hooked beak-jaw. It squirms through Sand Dune tunnels just below the surface, leaving winding channels that explorers call echo-burrows, because the trails it makes seem to form a pattern when viewed from a high dune. It eats nothing but sand grains and the compressed sunlight locked inside them.
stages.note: Chitling's burrow trails, viewed from the top of the nearest high dune, sometimes form a single clear spiral.

stages.name: Chitiderm
stages.bio: Chitiderm is entirely encased in a hard oval shell of burnished bronze-brown chitin, segmented in six horizontal bands. A faint orange glyph glows on its face-plate - the only sign of the creature resting inside. In the Sand Dunes it buries itself at the base of crescent dunes and waits, perfectly still, sometimes for weeks. Old sigils pressed into nearby sand tiles drift closer while it sleeps, as if drawn by the glow of its face-mark.
stages.note: Sand tiles within one body-length of a buried Chitiderm rotate slowly toward it over three days, as if being read.

stages.name: Chitoptera
stages.bio: Chitoptera is a massive upright beetle-warrior: bronze-brown wing-cases folded across a wide thorax, thick raking foreclaws, huge curved horn above its brow, and two powerful hind legs that carry it in bounding rushes across the dune field. Its carapace has hardened over a thousand moults and now deflects wind-whipped sand entirely. It carries every old sigil from its earlier burrows in its memory, and guards the dune boundary as if it were the last memory-keeper between the desert and the dark.
stages.note: Chitoptera can bound twelve body-lengths in one leap - its takeoff leaves a crater that fills with fine ripple-patterns.

stages.name: Acornit
stages.bio: Acornit is an upright acorn-bodied creature with a large ribbed cap, two bright round eyes, and a pair of small leafy fists held at its sides - each fist is a green-leafed pod it shakes when excited. It stands on two stubby legs and toddles along Granite Heights' lower paths at a determined pace, always counter-clockwise, as if memorizing the circuit. Axon the fish-guardian once used these same trails, and Acornit still follows that ancient route, marking the path for any child who wishes to learn it.
stages.note: Acornit always walks Granite Heights' lower circuit counter-clockwise, completing the loop in exactly 22 minutes regardless of obstacles.

stages.name: Conkarl
stages.bio: Conkarl has grown into a stocky upright fighter - its acorn-cap crown is now thick and ridged, its body is broad and banded in warm chestnut, and its fists have become knotted acorn-pod knuckles it can pound together to make a sound that carries the length of Granite Heights' ridge. It still walks the patrol route every morning, but now faster and wider, covering the mid-elevation paths that Axon once climbed. When it finds an old mark carved into the granite it traces it with one knuckle three times before continuing.
stages.note: Conkarl traces any old mark it finds carved in granite exactly three times with its knuckle, as if confirming the shape each pass.

stages.name: Terakhan
stages.bio: Terakhan is immense and ancient - an acorn-cap warrior grown to titan scale, its body wrapped in carved wooden armor and its great round crown cracked with age but unbroken. Its massive fists strike the granite path with such force that fresh sigils appear in the stone face. High in Granite Heights, where Axon the guardian first carved the learning-paths, Terakhan stands at the summit each dawn facing east, waiting with the patience of heartwood for the lost guardians to return and read the stone it has guarded since the shadow fell.
stages.note: Each strike of Terakhan's fist on summit granite leaves a fresh sigil - cartographers have mapped 300 of them attributed to it.

stages.name: Corayu
stages.bio: Corayu is a small blue sea-sprite with a round body, two wide eyes, and a bundle of bright orange coral-tendrils sprouting from its head like a cheerful crown. A simple anchor emblem is painted or grown on its round belly. In Amber Desert it is a curiosity - a water-creature thriving in the driest region - but it survives by finding the deep underground aquifers below the dunes and surfacing at dusk to bounce on the warm sand. It hums constantly while bouncing, marking each bounce with a different note.
stages.note: Corayu marks each bounce with a different note - researchers have recorded 140 distinct notes from one dusk session.

stages.name: Corlite
stages.bio: Corlite has grown into a broad, powerful sea-beast with a carapace of fused stone-coral, a spiked crown of orange-red coral ridges on its head, and a wide chest bearing a shield-like emblem. It stands on four solid legs and moves with patient deliberateness through the Amber Desert, using its coral-crown to dowse for underground water. When it finds a singing aquifer it marks it by pressing its chest-emblem against the ground, leaving a old seal in the sand that lasts a full moon before it fades.
stages.note: Corlite's chest-seal marks a singing aquifer for exactly one full moon - desert-walkers follow the fading seals like a memory-map.

stages.name: Corlith
stages.bio: Corlith is a fortress of living stone-coral - a broad-bodied warden whose shell and hide are entirely fused coral-rock, its crest a full array of jagged coral spires, and a massive flat shield grown into its chest as natural armour. It carries water inside its coral chambers, enough to sustain itself and three other creatures for a week in full desert heat. In the depths of Amber Desert it stands beside the oldest singing aquifer, patient since before the desert was a desert, waiting for the sea to come back to it.
stages.note: Corlith carries enough internal water to sustain itself for seven days of desert sun without any external source.

stages.name: Scuttlix
stages.bio: Scuttlix wears a cone-shaped pale-grey metallic shell like a knight's helmet that is slightly too big for it, tilting forward over round eyes that peer out with cautious optimism. Its orange-red legs are nimble and quick, and it can squeeze into crystal crevices no wider than a coin. In the Crystal Mines it collects flecks of ore, pressing them to the outside of its shell until the cone glitters. It greets every new learner by holding up one small claw in salute.
stages.note: Scuttlix adds exactly one ore fleck to its shell each day - researchers can tell its age by counting the layers.

stages.name: Clawmor
stages.bio: Clawmor has traded its cone shell for a broad hammered-steel carapace with riveted plates and a forward crest, and its once-orange legs are now a deep rust-red with reinforced joints. Its claws have grown wide and flat - perfect for prying ore veins open or bracing a tunnel entrance against collapse. The Crystal Mine's deep workers call it the Tunnel Warden; Clawmor knows every passage by echo, and moves through pitch-dark shafts without slowing.
stages.note: Clawmor navigates by tapping its claws and timing the echo - it has never walked into a wall.

stages.name: Titanyx
stages.bio: Titanyx stands upright like a fortress given legs, its entire body encased in massive orange-and-steel plating, with towering spine-crests along its back and hooked battle-claws that scrape sparks from the mine floor. Its eyes glow a steady amber behind heavy brow plates. The Crystal Mines were built around its territory - miners leave it an offering of raw ore each season, and in return it has never once collapsed a worked tunnel. It is both guardian and gatekeeper of what lies below.
stages.note: The footfall of a walking Titanyx registers on seismic instruments forty kilometers away.

stages.name: Crystkit
stages.bio: Crystkit is a fluffy white fox kit with a light-blue snowflake patch on its forehead and a thick curling tail tipped pale blue. Its four paws leave tiny star-shaped frost prints on the Frozen Peaks tidepools. It chases light refractions through the shallow water with a focus that looks almost scholarly - stopping dead whenever one lands perfectly on its snout. Locals say Crystkit is trying to bottle a sunbeam in ice, and one day it will succeed.
stages.note: Crystkit's breath crystallizes into a tiny six-pointed snowflake exactly once per exhale - no two are the same.

stages.name: Crystrail
stages.bio: Crystrail has grown graceful and swift, its white coat now shimmering with pale-blue runic patterns and a long swirling ice-plume tail that streams behind it in motion. A single ice-blue horn rises from its forehead, and when sunlight hits it, prismatic light scatters across the Frozen Peaks like dropped jewels. It races the tide in at dawn and races it back out, never wet, never caught - the peaks fishers call it the morning omen of a good fair wind.
stages.note: Crystrail runs at full speed across water surfaces without breaking the meniscus - scientists call it an unsolved pressure mystery.

stages.name: Crystalleigh
stages.bio: Crystalleigh is radiant - a large sleek fox with a full fan of crystalline tail-plumes that refract light into full spectrum arcs behind it, and glowing blue rune-markings etched across its body. Its eyes are deep sapphire, and when it stands still on the high ice shelf at sunrise, the light it throws is visible from the valley floor. Old Frozen Peaks tales say it was spun from the first ray of morning that ever touched the snow.
stages.note: The light-fan of a resting Crystalleigh projects stable prismatic patterns across 200 square meters of snowfield.

stages.name: Frostpip
stages.bio: Frostpip is a tiny round white owlet with a small cluster of blue ice-crystal tufts atop its head like a crown it didn't ask for, and large turquoise eyes that glow faintly in the dark. It perches on the frost-cracked rock shelves of Frozen Peaks, staring into the meltpool below with enormous seriousness. Every few minutes it blinks slowly and the water beneath it briefly freezes into a perfect disc that thaws almost immediately, leaving the local fish thoroughly confused.
stages.note: Frostpip blinks once every 47 seconds exactly; researchers have used it to synchronize field watches.

stages.name: Glacier
stages.bio: Glacier is a handsome owl, upright and cool-toned, with pale-blue plumage marked by a crescent moon symbol on its chest and layered wing-feathers that each hold a faint ice shimmer. Its eyes have deepened to a penetrating teal, and it rotates its head in full circles slowly when processing information - something researchers describe as watching a very patient machine think. It haunts the Frozen Peaks tidal caves, and its silent passage through a cave mouth always precedes an unusual tide.
stages.note: Glacier solves visual puzzles placed in its territory overnight - field notes describe complex stick arrangements rearranged before dawn.

stages.name: Ethereowl
stages.bio: Ethereowl spreads wings of layered ice-crystal feathers so thin light passes through them in prismatic sheets, and its body is pale as sea-fog with runic patterning glowing along the wing edges. Its eyes are deep teal - ancient, knowing - and it holds its gaze for so long that subjects report feeling their most recent difficult question answered without sounds. It circles Frozen Peaks at high tide, reading the sea as a text, and the fishers say whatever it circles will surface by morning.
stages.note: Ethereowl's wing-feathers shed one at each new moon; each shed feather is found arranged in a circle around its roost by morning.

stages.name: Embpup
stages.bio: Embpup is a compact black fox kit with a fiery orange-tipped tuft on its head and burning ember-orange eyes that glow in the dark of the Shadow Caves. Its fur is jet-black with faint dark-charcoal patterning, and thin flame-wisps lick upward from its ears and collar fur when it is excited. It navigates the caves entirely by heat-sense, padding through passages with absolute confidence even in total darkness. It will curl against the chest of any sleeping traveler, providing warmth and unsettling dreams in equal measure.
stages.note: Embpup's ear-flames burn hotter when it hears a lie - Shadow Cave travelers use it as an impromptu truth detector.

stages.name: Emberuine
stages.bio: Emberuine is a powerful lean dark fox with a collar of persistent flames wreathing its neck and shoulders, and a tail that burns at the tip with a steady, unwavering flame. Its paws leave scorched claw-marks on stone, and its eyes now glow with volcanic intensity. In the Shadow Caves it is neither guide nor threat - it simply claims a territory at the point where the dark meets the warmth, and anything that crosses that line without announcement answers for it. Trainers say it respects courage above all.
stages.note: The flame-collar of Emberuine burns brighter when its trainer achieves something genuinely difficult - a documented behavioral response to mastery.

stages.name: Infernak
stages.bio: Infernak is extraordinary - a massive black-furred beast wreathed in persistent flame that burns from its collar, mane, tail, and each paw-strike, trailing fire in its wake. Its body is sculpted and powerful, and its orange-fire eyes carry a depth that suggests it has seen the Shadow Caves' oldest secrets. It is the keeper of the boundary between the burning world and the lightless world, and the guardians' texts describe it as a creature that chose neither light nor dark alone - but the fierce, necessary meeting point between them.
stages.note: A sleeping Infernak keeps its flame burning at precisely the minimum level to prevent cave-freeze - local creatures shelter within its heat radius.

stages.name: Sparkbit
stages.bio: Sparkbit is a grey-and-black wolf pup with a short spiky mohawk of black fur and bright amber eyes that arc tiny static sparks when it blinks in dry air. Its body is compact and low-slung, and it trots through the Sand Dunes leaving a trail of tiny singed-sand dots - static discharges with every step. It forms a small pack with any creature nearby, regardless of species, assigning itself the role of scout and then running so far ahead that it forgets what it was scouting for.
stages.note: Sparkbit cannot stop producing static in dry dune air - it is permanently slightly on fire and completely unbothered by this.

stages.name: Blazemark
stages.bio: Blazemark has grown into a striking dark wolf with a dramatic spiky red-and-orange crest running from its skull to mid-back, like a living flame crest. Its coat is dark grey-black with ember-red markings, and electric crackling runs along its spine during a charge. In the Sand Dunes it runs the long dune ridgelines at dusk, and sand-traders navigating after sunset use the crackling visible from its crest as a distant landmark. It has been described as a moving fire-signal that also occasionally bites.
stages.note: The electric-fire crest of Blazemark is visible from 5 kilometers in darkness; dune traders have it on their navigation charts.

stages.name: Inferfang
stages.bio: Inferfang is a legend made flesh - a colossal wolf armored in dark ridged plating with full wings of fire and electricity erupting from its shoulders and flanks, a blazing crest from skull to tail-base, and eyes that burn like twin forge-fires. When it runs across the Sand Dunes, the sand beneath it fuses to glass. The Abalont texts say it was made from the first thunderstorm that ever crossed the desert - that it is the sound of lightning learning to run on four legs and finding it preferred that to falling.
stages.note: Inferfang's footprints in sand fuse to glass; a trail of hexagonal glass discs across a dune is the only record of its passage.

stages.name: Embix
stages.bio: Embix is a compact, round-bodied fire-bird with wide flapping orange-red wings and fierce round eyes. Its crest of flame-feathers blazes from its crown, and it hops along the lip of the Lava Crater, wings spread wide, practicing its balance against the updrafts. It cannot yet sustain flight for more than a minute but compensates by hurling tiny fire-sparks from its beak with startling accuracy. The crater's heat is its cradle - it hatches from lava-warmed rock.
stages.note: Embix hops exactly twelve times before it attempts flight - trainers have counted, and it never varies.

stages.name: Pyreion
stages.bio: Pyreion soars above the Lava Crater on wide swept wings of deep orange and gold, its tail-feathers streaming fire behind it. Its entire body radiates heat like a second sun, and passing through its wake leaves a warm tingling on skin. It circles the crater in long lazy loops, watching for cooling lava bridges to land on. Its cry at dusk tells the creatures below that the crater is safe for another night - silence from a Pyreion is a warning worth heeding.
stages.note: Pyreion's tail-flame streams longer behind it when it is carrying good news - explorers gauge fortune by the length.

stages.name: Solpyre
stages.bio: Solpyre is a towering fire-dragon-phoenix, its great wings wrapped in roaring orange flame and its coiled body armored with thick fire-scales. Its neck curves with serpentine power, and its talons grip stone as if born from it. When it spreads its wings above the Lava Crater at sunrise, the reflected fire lights the entire surrounding highlands orange-gold. The guardians recorded this creature at the crater's founding: the original flame that will never be extinguished, reborn from every eruption.
stages.note: Solpyre sheds one flame-feather each year at midsummer - the feather burns for exactly one year, no more.

stages.name: Cindercub
stages.bio: Cindercub is a small orange-and-red canine pup with a spiky flame-mane beginning to sprout along its neck. Its compact body is covered in fire-touched fur, and its tail flicks with tiny embers. It digs shallow burrows in the Sand Dunes at dawn before the heat grows unbearable, filling them with warm sand to sleep in. It chirps at the other dune creatures with its tiny voice, and the locals say you can smell its warm fur long before you spot it.
stages.note: Cindercub's flame-mane points toward water beneath the sand - dune tribes follow it during droughts.

stages.name: Blazarc
stages.bio: Blazarc is a lean, long-legged fire-beast with a full spiky blaze-mane and a body of fire-orange layered fur. Its legs are built for long desert strides, and its narrow head turns quickly to scan the horizon. When the sandstorms roll in from the deep desert, Blazarc is the first to face them - it stands at the dune-crest and lets the wind fuel its mane until the blaze is visible for half a league. Nomad children follow its mane-light to safety.
stages.note: Blazarc's mane-fire gives off no smoke and no heat beyond arm's length - safe enough to sleep beside in a storm.

stages.name: Infernarch
stages.bio: Infernarch stands vast and fierce with a full volcanic mane of jagged fire-spikes that crown its entire upper body. Its thick fire-fur armor covers broad shoulders, and its massive paws carry claws that score deep grooves in sandstone. When it raises its head and howls at the desert moon, its mane-fire reflects off the dunes in a ring of amber light visible from the desert's edge. It is the guardian flame of the Sand Dunes, the fire-road marker the ancient travelers prayed to.
stages.note: Infernarch's roar travels exactly one league through desert air - the unit of measure was defined by its cry.

stages.name: Emblkit
stages.bio: Emblkit is a blue-grey kitten with warm amber eyes, stubby orange-tipped ears, and a small tail that curls upward. A shy creature of the Dark Forest, it hides behind gnarled roots and watches travelers through the gloom with those luminous eyes - never quite trusting, never quite leaving. It was noticed by the early guardians because it would follow them to the forest's edge, then turn back. Something in the Dark Forest calls it home, even as the hero-blood in its veins pulls it forward.
stages.note: Emblkit's eyes reflect light in a unique two-color split - left eye gold, right eye silver - which never reverses.

stages.name: Emblicat
stages.bio: Emblicat has grown large and powerfully built, its blue-grey fur now deeply shadowed with dark markings and its body low-slung and muscular. Thick orange-tipped ears alert to every sound, and its amber eyes glow in the forest dark. It has taken on a guardian role in the Dark Forest, standing between the deepest shadows and the creatures that live on the light side. Its roar keeps the darkness at bay - the guardians say one Emblicat patrolling is worth three sentry posts.
stages.note: Emblicat places its right paw on the ground at a trail's fork - the side it rests on is always the safer path.

stages.name: Emblion
stages.bio: Emblion is a vast, broad-shouldered dark lion whose mane blazes in deep navy-purple shadow-fire. Its body is pure muscle under dark-sapphire fur, and its wide amber eyes carry centuries of forest memory. When Abalont's shadow crept deepest into the Dark Forest, Emblion stood at the boundary and refused to move for seven days. The forest remembers. Every tree in the Dark Forest grows slightly bent toward wherever Emblion last walked - following its guardian.
stages.note: Emblion always faces east at dawn - the direction it once watched for the guardians' return.

stages.name: Flambat
stages.bio: Flambat is a small dusk-furred bat with faintly glowing wing-membranes that flicker like banked embers when it is excited. It roosts upside down in the wind-cut hollows of Gale Ridge and squeaks in bursts of three, which the locals say means 'again, again, again' - it never tires of anything.
stages.note: Flambat squeaks in groups of exactly three - more than three means danger; fewer means it is just saying hello.

stages.name: Pyrewing
stages.bio: Pyrewing has grown into a solidly built dark-blue bat-beast with wide leathery wings and a bold orange-spiked crest. Its wings now span wide enough to ride the storm-winds of Gale Ridge without effort, and it navigates by a combination of echolocation and electrical sensing. It swoops through the tower's upper arches at night, shedding dark wind-gusts that extinguish torches below. Travelers on Gale Ridge mark Pyrewing's patrol paths on maps - it is the safest guide through a tempest.
stages.note: Pyrewing's wing-beats are perfectly timed to the gap between lightning strikes - it never gets struck.

stages.name: Pyrebat
stages.bio: Pyrebat is a powerful dark bat-dragon with enormous swept wings and a fierce spiked head-crest that glows amber in lightning flashes. Its body is broad and muscular, covered in dark-blue armored hide. At the peak of Gale Ridge, where the winds never stop, it nests. When a true storm arrives, it spreads its wings and becomes the storm - hovering motionless at the spire's pinnacle while the gale pours off its wingtips. The spire would be impassable without it absorbing the worst gusts.
stages.note: Pyrebat drinks lightning through its crest-spikes and releases it slowly as sustained body-warmth for three days.

stages.name: Embysaur
stages.bio: Embysaur is a small purple-scaled lizard with a stubby rounded body, large amber eyes, and a tiny wisp of smoke curling from its nostril. It hatches from eggs laid in the Lava Crater's cooler rock-pockets and immediately begins licking the warm mineral residue off the basalt. Its round belly is always full of something, and it tilts its head to one side whenever it hears a name it has never heard, as if filing it somewhere important. The guardians first catalogued it as 'the one that always looks confused but never gets lost.'
stages.note: Embysaur always licks the same rock seven times before deciding whether it is edible - seven is its number.

stages.name: Pyrolisk
stages.bio: Pyrolisk stands upright on powerful hind legs, its purple-scaled body now broader and covered in glowing orange lava-spots that pulse with heat. It walks the mid-crater, navigating the hot stone ridges on long strong hind legs while its shorter forelimbs swing for balance. Its tail sweeps the ground behind it, clearing its own path through loose cinder. The orange spots on its flanks glow brightest at the moments when it scents new magma rising - giving minutes of warning before a new vent opens.
stages.note: Pyrolisk's orange spots pulse seven times per minute at rest and up to forty times per minute near active lava.

stages.name: Infernathor
stages.bio: Infernathor is a vast winged purple-dragon covered in overlapping fire-scale plates, its back and wings ablaze with orange lava-glow that illuminates the entire crater bowl at night. Its wings spread wide as the crater's rim, and when it beats them the lava below ripples. Its thick neck curves with a dragon's ancient authority, and its lava-spot markings have merged into a continuous blazing pattern across its flanks. The Lava Crater was not made by the volcano alone - the guardians say Infernathor chose it and settled there, and the mountain grew up around it.
stages.note: Infernathor breathes once every four minutes - a fact that Lava Crater explorers use to time safe crossings of the crater floor.

stages.name: Floret
stages.bio: Floret is little more than a cheerful yellow body with three wide leaf-wings fanning out on each side, making it look more like a flying flower than an insect. Two short antennae bob as it hovers at low altitude, and its tiny round eyes study every passing leaf with great concentration. It lives in the Bug Thicket's sunlit glades, feeding on pollen dust that drifts between the canopy gaps. Floret moves in tight loops, tasting the air, and always finds its way home even when it wanders far.
stages.note: Floret can hover motionless for up to four minutes while it decides whether a particular flower petal is worth landing on.

stages.name: Florant
stages.bio: Florant has grown a longer armored yellow-gold body and its leaf-wings have narrowed into sharper blades, buzzing at a frequency that makes nearby grass hum sympathetically. It now hunts fast, darting between trunks in the Bug Thicket like a living arrow, tracking the subtle scents left by ripe seed-clusters. Its antennae have extended and curve back along its body, and its mandibles have hardened enough to score bark. Experienced Thicket guides say a grove guarded by Florant never loses a tree to blight.
stages.note: When Florant's wings beat at full speed, the vibration shakes loose exactly the seeds it wants to eat - the rest stay on the stem.

stages.name: Floravant
stages.bio: Floravant is a heavy-bodied gold-green insect with broad overlapping leaf-blade wings and thick segmented armor plating. Its clawed legs grip bark like a vice, and when it spreads its full wingspan, the canopy around it goes still - smaller insects stop flying and leaves flatten. It patrols the Bug Thicket's oldest trees, repairing damaged bark with resin it produces itself, and its buzzing presence drives off anything that would cut or burn the grove. Guardians left a small carving of Floravant at every old tree in the thicket as a marker of protection.
stages.note: Floravant can seal a wound in a tree's bark within two hours using a resin it secretes from glands behind its mandibles.

stages.name: Frondlet
stages.bio: Frondlet is a small bright-green creature that sits upright like a vigilant lizard, with a row of pointy green spikes running from its crown down its back. Its large golden eyes and slightly grumpy expression give it the look of a tiny creature taking itself very seriously. Found in the sunny clearings of Verdant Valley where the grass grows tall, it spends most of its time sitting perfectly still among the stems, listening. When it does move, every motion is precise and deliberate - this creature has never taken a careless step.
stages.note: Frondlet's back-spikes each point a different direction when wind shifts, mapping gusts across the valley floor more accurately than any weather vane.

stages.name: Frondarch
stages.bio: Frondarch has grown into a powerfully built four-legged dragon with ridged green-gold plating across its back and a spiral leaf-marking etched into its flank like a natural sigil. Its spines have grown longer and harder, and the deep golden eyes now carry a spark of genuine fire. It walks the outer edges of Verdant Valley where the grass meets the wilder undergrowth, marking territory with scratches on stones. Other grass-creatures give it a respectful distance - not because Frondarch is aggressive, but because it radiates a quiet certainty that takes up space.
stages.note: Frondarch can bite through a vine as thick as a wrist in one snap and immediately weaves the halves back together into a tighter knot than before.

stages.name: Frondyrant
stages.bio: Frondyrant is a massive quadruped dragon covered in thick overlapping plates of dark green armor, each plate edged in gold. Its spine is now a continuous ridge of great curved horns, and the swirling vine-sigil on its flank has expanded to cover most of its side in luminous green spiral patterns. It settles at the heart of Verdant Valley each season-change and the valley's plants seem to grow faster, taller, and greener in a circle around its resting spot. Guardians who knew it as a hatchling still bring it exactly three leaves of sweet clover as a greeting - it accepts them with great solemnity.
stages.note: Every plant within ten meters of a resting Frondyrant grows at twice its normal rate, including weeds, which Frondyrant finds mildly undignified.

stages.name: Frondyte
stages.bio: Frondyte is a small upright lizard-type creature covered in bright green spines from crown to tail tip. Its large golden eyes regard the world with a calm, measuring look far older than its small body suggests. It hatches near the outer cool-stone ring of the Lava Crater where green mosses manage to grow despite the heat, and it spends its days eating those mosses while the crater's warmth radiates up through the rock beneath it. The combination of volcanic mineral-soil and cool green growth gives this hatchling a constitution that surprises everything that tries to outrun it.
stages.note: Frondyte's spines absorb volcanic mineral steam from the crater air; each spine contains trace amounts of obsidian that crystallizes slowly over its lifetime.

stages.name: Frondax
stages.bio: Frondax is a lean, aggressive lizard-dragon whose green spines have grown long and blade-edged, running in multiple rows down its back and flanks. Small tusks curve upward from its lower jaw, and its tail is thick and spiked. It patrols the transition zone of the Lava Crater where basalt stone meets scattered grass, hunting insects that cluster on the warm rock-faces. The heat seems to energize rather than exhaust it, and it can sprint across a scorching rock field that would burn any unarmored foot.
stages.note: Frondax can climb sheer basalt walls using only the edges of its flank-spines as grips, and descends facing forward - a rare combination of agility and nerve.

stages.name: Frondsaur
stages.bio: Frondsaur is a formidable full-grown dragon whose body is a tapestry of long green spines, swept-back horns, and muscled limbs that look carved from the crater's oldest basalt. Its wings are broad and fern-patterned, built as much for gliding the crater's thermal columns as for powered flight. Where it rests at night, a ring of surprisingly lush grass springs up by morning, fed by the mineral-rich residue its scales leave on rock surfaces. Lava Crater settlers speak of Frondsaur with respect: it is the only thing that grows greener the closer it gets to the fire.
stages.note: Frondsaur's shed scales are used by crater-side herbalists as the only planting substrate in which crater-edge herbs will reliably germinate.

stages.name: Chillpup
stages.bio: Chillpup looks harmless enough - a soft blue-white pup with wide round eyes and a fluffy tail - but the Crystal Mines have left their mark on it. Its fur carries a faint metallic sheen, and it is far quicker to growl than to wag. It has learned to use the darkness between crystal formations to hide with uncanny skill, its pale coat blending with the frost-rimed walls in a way that makes miners nervous. Small enough to sit in a lap but sharp enough to bite a boot clean through, Chillpup is not a creature to underestimate.
stages.note: Chillpup can vanish between two crystal columns in less than a heartbeat - miners call this vanishing trick the "cold blink."

stages.name: Glacière
stages.bio: Glacière has shed its puppy roundness entirely, replacing it with lean, angular muscle and a bristling mane of sharp ice spikes along its spine that rattle faintly when it moves. Long curved fangs extend below its jaw, and its eyes have sharpened from round innocence to a focused, calculating cold. It hunts through the Crystal Mines by listening for the faint sound of crystal resonance, tracking prey by the vibrations their footsteps make in the stone. Its territory is marked not by scent but by hairline frost cracks left in the walls.
stages.note: Glacière can hear a single drop of water falling from the mine ceiling from over sixty meters away through solid stone.

stages.name: Blizzaroch
stages.bio: Blizzaroch fills the mine corridors like a storm filling a valley. Rows of enormous ice spikes line its back and flanks, and deep scar-lines across its hide tell of ancient battles fought before any current guardian was born. Its massive jaws open to reveal fangs the length of pickaxes. When Blizzaroch howls, frost forms instantly on every nearby crystal, and the temperature in the mines drops so fast that breath freezes before it leaves the mouth. The Crystal Mines belong to Blizzaroch - everything else in them is simply a guest.
stages.note: The ice spikes along Blizzaroch's back never melt, even when carried out of the mines into summer heat - they simply grow colder.

stages.name: Sporite
stages.bio: Sporite is a tiny round mushroom creature with a smooth brown cap and big wide eyes that blink slowly and independently of each other. Its two stumpy legs shuffle it along the sand with surprising speed for something so round, and tiny spore puffs drift from its cap whenever it hops. Despite living in the Sand Dunes, Sporite thrives where underground moisture seeps up between the dunes, forming small oasis patches that only it can find. Young Sporites are born in clusters of three, and they spend their first weeks following each other in circles.
stages.note: The spores Sporite releases each morning contain a faint sweet smell that attracts underground beetles - which then aerate the soil and help moisture travel upward.

stages.name: Myconaut
stages.bio: Myconaut stands upright now on two solid legs, its broad flat mushroom cap casting a wide shadow over its compact body. It has short sturdy arms it keeps crossed in front of its chest, giving it an air of permanent skepticism. The cap has widened and flattened, and it releases a visible cloud of spores when startled that can put small creatures to sleep for a few hours - a trick it uses to negotiate rather than fight. Myconaut has been spotted at ancient memory-stone sites throughout the Sand Dunes, seemingly reading the carvings.
stages.note: Myconaut is always found within forty meters of an underground water source, even in the driest dune fields - it has never once been wrong.

stages.name: Fungolith
stages.bio: Fungolith is ancient beyond reckoning - more root system than creature now, with thick twisted root-legs that drive deep into the sand and draw water from aquifers no other being has reached. Its trunk-like body is scored with bark, and its massive mushroom cap shelters an entire ecosystem of smaller creatures beneath it. When it speaks, the vibration travels through the ground as much as through the air, and sand dunes shift slightly in response. The oldest oases in the dunes were not natural - they formed beneath a resting Fungolith.
stages.note: Fungolith has never moved more than ten meters in recorded history - but the sand dunes around it have slowly reshaped over centuries to face it.

stages.name: Sporkit
stages.bio: Sporkit is a tiny round turtle with a smooth mushroom-cap growing from the top of its shell, spotted in warm tan and brown. Its four stubby limbs barely lift it off the ground, and it spends most of its time sitting perfectly still on rocky outcroppings of Granite Heights, absorbing warmth and moisture with equal contentment. It can pull its head and all four legs in at once, leaving only the mushroom cap visible - which makes it look remarkably like an ordinary toadstool until it decides to move.
stages.note: Sporkit's mushroom cap changes color slightly with weather - it darkens before rain, even in the usually-dry heights.

stages.name: Fungrok
stages.bio: Fungrok's mushroom cap shell has grown large enough to shelter its entire body, spotted tan and brown with a frill of pale spores along the edge. It sits upright now with a broad flat face and watchful eyes, moving only when necessary - and never faster than a stroll. The granite outcroppings of the Heights are dotted with resting Fungroks that look indistinguishable from boulders to the untrained eye. When multiple Fungroks gather in the same area, their cap spores combine to create a gentle sleep-haze that settles over the rocks like mist.
stages.note: Fungrok has been recorded sitting motionless in the same spot for eleven consecutive days - it emerged only when the sun finally moved fully off its rock.

stages.name: Fungshell
stages.bio: Fungshell has grown into a massive squat tortoise nearly as wide as it is tall, its mushroom-cap shell expanded into a wide flat canopy that acts as a true roof when it hunkers down. Its skin has thickened into warty plated hide, and a thick ring of root-like tendrils hangs from the cap's edge, anchoring it to the ground when it sleeps. Granite Heights locals have built rest shelters near Fungshell nesting sites because the creature's presence keeps dangerous rockslides from reaching paths below - its weight and roots stabilize the slopes.
stages.note: When a Fungshell sneezes - which happens roughly once a month - the spore cloud it releases can fog an entire mountainside for half a day.

stages.name: Geodite
stages.bio: Geodite is a small black-shelled turtle covered in raised golden studs that serve as electrical contact points. It moves with quiet confidence through the Steel Fortress, drawn to active machinery by the faint electric fields it detects through its stud-covered shell. Its dark carapace absorbs no light - at night, only the golden studs are visible, giving it the look of a miniature starscape. It has learned to recharge itself by pressing its shell against the fortress's generator housings, and maintenance crews have found that Geodite-rested generators need less servicing.
stages.note: Each golden stud on Geodite's shell is a separate electrical node - they can fire independently, which means it can release charge from any angle simultaneously.

stages.name: Gedonyx
stages.bio: Gedonyx has grown into a formidable dark-armored tortoise with golden spikes now rising from its shell like lightning rods, and a single prominent horn extending forward from its head. When it senses an approaching storm, every golden spike on its body begins to glow with accumulated charge. The Steel Fortress relies on Gedonyx herds in the outer wall corridors as living surge protectors - during lightning strikes, the creatures absorb excess charge and distribute it safely through their contact with the stone floor. They are fed and housed by the Fortress in return.
stages.note: Gedonyx can absorb up to four consecutive lightning strikes without discharging - on the fifth strike, it releases everything at once in a single directed bolt.

stages.name: Gedomancer
stages.bio: Gedomancer is the Steel Fortress's most ancient resident, a creature so laden with stored electrical charge that arc lightning jumps between its shell spikes continuously in dry weather. Its dark armored body is broad as a siege vehicle, its golden spikes now the size of large spears, and the horn on its head has grown long enough to serve as a deliberate lightning rod when it wishes to draw a bolt down from the sky. On the night of the great storm three centuries ago, a Gedomancer stood at the fortress's highest point and absorbed the entire storm, leaving the fortress untouched.
stages.note: Gedomancer has never once been struck by lightning - it has always been what lightning strikes instead.

stages.name: Peblin
stages.bio: Peblin is a tiny round grey pebble creature with large cheerful eyes and a single blue ice-crystal spike growing from the top of its head like a frozen horn. It bounces rather than walks, each hop leaving a tiny frost ring on the stone surface it lands on. Peblin lives on the exposed rock faces of Frozen Peaks where the wind is strongest and temperatures drop below freezing before midnight. It seems to enjoy the cold entirely too much - turning its tiny crystal spike to face into the wind and holding still with what can only be described as bliss.
stages.note: Peblin's crystal spike grows three millimeters for every degree below freezing - at the spire's peak, researchers have recorded spikes forty centimeters long.

stages.name: Geolith
