stages.bio: Geolith has transformed entirely - from a round hopping pebble into an upright bipedal warrior with broad stone-plated fists, a chest covered in jagged ice-crystal armor, and a crown of large blue ice spikes jutting from its head and shoulders. It is not graceful, but it is nearly indestructible. Geolith patrols the mid-level ledges of Frozen Peaks, where lightning strikes the stone often enough to melt and refreeze the ice crystals on its body in constant renewal. It braces against the wind with its wide flat feet and never loses its footing.
stages.note: Geolith has been struck by lightning forty-six times in observed history - each strike appears to fuse more crystal onto its body rather than damaging it.

stages.name: Crystallax
stages.bio: Crystallax has transcended its rocky origins - its body is now encased in gleaming golden-bronze armor with a massive crown of enormous blue ice-crystal spires radiating from its shoulders and head like a frozen sun. Each ice crystal in the crown is a different shade of blue, from pale powder to deep glacial, and they catch lightning and scatter it harmlessly into the storm clouds. At the Frozen Peaks' absolute peak, Crystallax stands facing the wind without flinching, arms spread, during the most violent storms - explorers have watched it for hours from the shelter of the lower rocks below.
stages.note: When Crystallax extends its arms fully during a storm, the lightning always strikes the highest crystal spike and travels down through its body into the bedrock below, never entering the spire itself.

stages.name: Crystelle
stages.bio: Crystelle spends its early life as a closed oyster shell resting at the bottom of Poison Marsh's quieter pools, its two grey-white shells sealed tight around a glowing blue crystal gem it has been growing since before it was born. A ring of faint blue light seeps from the shell's seam when the gem inside pulses. It is perfectly still for days at a time, filtering toxins from the marsh water through its steel-hard shells and locking them away inside its crystalline core. Marsh ecologists believe Crystelle seedlings are responsible for the marsh's clean-water pockets appearing exactly where they are most needed.
stages.note: The blue gem growing inside each Crystelle contains no toxins despite filtering marsh water constantly - it converts them entirely into crystal mass.

stages.name: Shellume
stages.bio: Shellume has cracked open and emerged as a multi-legged crustacean with a pale armored body, six jointed legs tipped with steel-hard points, and a rough domed shell that has absorbed enough metal from the marsh minerals to ring like a bell when struck. A single large blue eye sits above its wide mouth. It walks upside-down on the ceiling of underwater rock formations for days, filtering the water overhead and occasionally dropping crystals that accumulate into formations on the marsh floor below. Researchers mapping the marsh use Shellume crystal deposits as waypoints.
stages.note: Shellume's blue eye can see through murky water as clearly as clean air - marsh explorers claim following one through a fog bank leads to the shortest route every single time.

stages.name: Geomaxon
stages.bio: Geomaxon is massive and ancient, a hulking armored crab-golem whose body segments are thick steel-hard shell plates worn smooth by centuries in the marsh. A single enormous eye glows deep blue from its broad face, and its wide body is ringed with gold-hued detail lines like welded seams on a forged vessel. Its eight legs are powerful enough to walk on the marsh floor during high water, displacing everything nearby with its slow movement. Geomaxon anchors the Poison Marsh's deepest channels - its body is old enough that the entire marsh has reshaped around where it chooses to rest.
stages.note: The gold ring markings on Geomaxon's shell are the only part that is not natural - they were etched by an unknown hand in an age before recorded history, and they have never faded.

stages.name: Shellail
stages.bio: Shellail is the smallest creature of the Poison Marsh - a tiny pale blue snail with a perfectly round smooth shell and a soft round body that retracts instantly at the faintest vibration. It leaves a trail of faintly chilled water behind it as it glides through the shallows, and wherever that trail passes, the marsh water clears and the algae thins. Despite being tiny enough to sit on a large leaf without bending it, Shellail is found in some of the marsh's most dangerous spots, seemingly unbothered by the toxins around it. Marsh children collect empty Shellail shells as good-luck tokens.
stages.note: Shellail's trail clears an exact thirty-centimeter-wide stripe of algae - so uniform that marsh children use Shellail paths to navigate to the safe swimming spots.

stages.name: Frostshell
stages.bio: Frostshell has grown noticeably larger with a more elaborate shell - its smooth spiral now bears a beautiful snowflake pattern in pale blue and white that shimmers when it moves. Its body has taken on a deeper blue, and the trail it leaves is actually cold enough now to feel on bare skin. When threatened, Frostshell withdraws entirely into its shell and releases a ring of freezing water vapor that crystallizes on nearby surfaces in seconds, creating a small frost barrier. Marsh travelers have learned to spot Frostshell's distinctive snowflake-patterned shells from a distance and adjust their routes to use the cleared water it leaves.
stages.note: Frostshell always travels in a perfect spiral - start at any point in its trail and follow it inward and you will find where it spent the night.

stages.name: Crystail
stages.bio: Crystail is a magnificent sight in the grey-green marsh - a large snail with a crystallized spiral shell whose surface has frozen into angular facets, topped by a small crown of ice crystals that has grown from the shell's apex like a tiny glacier. Its body is a rich deep blue, and it moves with slow majestic purpose, never hurrying, never flinching. The marsh's clear-water channels all connect back to paths that Crystail has traveled repeatedly over centuries. It is believed that the Poison Marsh does not poison its own water simply because Crystail has been filtering it since before the marsh was named.
stages.note: The ice crystal crown on Crystail's shell has been photographed from above and below - from directly above, it forms the oldest known sigil, though scholars disagree on what it means.

stages.name: Glacisp
stages.bio: Glacisp is a tiny floating blue teardrop spirit - a round translucent body with a pointed tail that flickers like a candle flame and two wide pale eyes that seem to look in slightly different directions at once. It drifts through the fog-banks of Ghost Hollow barely disturbing the air, leaving a faint trail of cold mist. No one is certain whether it is the spirit of something that was once alive or a piece of the Hollow itself that learned to move. It collects cold air in its body and releases it as brief freezing puffs when startled.
stages.note: Glacisp is always slightly colder than the surrounding air - by exactly 3 degrees, always exactly 3.

stages.name: Glacivor
stages.bio: Glacivor has expanded into a ragged, billowing form - a mass of jagged icy-blue ghost-tendrils radiating from a glowing central core with pale hollow eyes. It moves through solid objects in Ghost Hollow, and the temperature drops sharply wherever it passes. It has no fixed shape for more than a moment, constantly reshaping its frozen vapour tendrils. The hollow's older spirits give it a wide berth, and even Abalont's shadows hesitate at the edges of the freezing aura it projects - cold cuts shadow more cleanly than light.
stages.note: Temperature drops by 6 degrees within one metre of Glacivor - researchers use it as a portable thermometer.

stages.name: Glaciathor
stages.bio: Glaciathor is an immense and terrible frozen phantom - a vast billowing form of jagged ice and ghost-fire filling most of the upper Ghost Hollow, its face a massive pale-glowing snarl of fangs and hollow eyes. Tendrils of frozen energy pour from it in every direction and the hollow's temperatures plunge below anything natural when it fully manifests. Ancient guardian texts describe it as the ghost of the glacier that once covered all the lands before Abalont's first shadow-summer - a memory of cold so deep it refused to end.
stages.note: Glaciathor's oldest ice-tendrils contain air bubbles from before the first words were ever written.

stages.name: Glacix
stages.bio: Glacix is a scrappy, pointy-eared ice-grey wolf pup with a wild mane of spiky fur that sticks up in every direction and keen amber eyes. Small ice-crystal studs dot its scruff and flanks. It prowls the upper tunnels of the Crystal Mines, sniffing out new crystal deposits by following temperature changes in the rock. It has the habit of howling at fresh crystals when it finds one, which makes it easy to find but loud to travel with. The mine-guardians have learned to give it space - every crystal it announces is worth excavating.
stages.note: Glacix can detect a new crystal deposit by smell through 15 centimetres of solid rock.

stages.name: Frostmane
stages.bio: Frostmane has grown into a powerful, athletic wolf with a broad chest, thick spiky silver-blue mane studded with crystal formations, and ice-plate armour growing along its spine. A crystal emblem glows on its sternum. It runs the deep shafts of the Crystal Mines in long fluid strides, checking every tunnel it mapped as a pup. When it finds a collapsed passage it pins the location with a howl pattern that the miners have learned to decode precisely - one long, two short means structural failure; three short means crystal bloom.
stages.note: Frostmane's tunnel-warning calls are so specific that mine engineers have written a formal translation guide based on them.

stages.name: Cryofang
stages.bio: Cryofang is an imposing wolf-like titan - massive, dark blue-grey body armoured in interlocking crystal plates that erupt from every joint and shoulder, its enormous mane a cascade of crystal shards that ring softly with each step. Its eyes blaze with cold crystalline fire and its paws leave faint crystal flowers in the rock wherever it walks. The Crystal Mines themselves seem older where Cryofang has been - as if its presence ages the crystals, deepening their colour and clarity. Ancient mine texts call it the Lord of the Vein.
stages.note: Any crystal that Cryofang has rested against grows 30% larger than surrounding crystals over the following year.

stages.name: Graxlet
stages.bio: Graxlet is a plump purple gecko no bigger than a fist, with wide golden eyes that catch every flicker of light in the dark tunnels. Its smooth violet body has subtle ridges along the back, and its thick tail curls with nervous energy. It clings to cave walls by tiny adhesive toes and licks the air to taste traces of visitors before they know it is there. In the shadow caves, Graxlet is the first sign that deeper, older things are watching.
stages.note: Graxlet tastes the air with a forked tongue flick every three seconds, even while asleep.

stages.name: Graxorm
stages.bio: Graxorm's body has lengthened and muscled up, with a row of sharp bony spines erupting along its backbone from neck to tail-tip. The purple scales have deepened toward violet-black on its sides, and its golden eyes now carry a shrewd gleam. It moves in slow, deliberate strides, pressing its belly low to the cave floor so its spines scrape the ceiling when it squeezes through narrow passages - a sound explorers learn to dread. Its toxic saliva leaves faint glowing smears on stone.
stages.note: The spine-scrape sound Graxorm makes on cave ceilings is said to echo for a full minute in deep chambers.

stages.name: Graxarch
stages.bio: Graxarch stands fully upright on powerful haunches, its spine-ridge now a crown of long gold-tipped horns that catch the faint light of the shadow caves. Its broad chest gleams with deep purple armored scales, and its thick tail sweeps the ground like a war-club. It exhales slow plumes of poisonous mist with each breath, and the cave walls nearest its lair are permanently stained a sickly violet. Guardians say Graxarch has memorized every voice ever raised in its domain and remembers slights for centuries.
stages.note: Graxarch marks its territory by exhaling a slow mist ring - the ring stays intact for hours in still cave air.

stages.name: Tidrop
stages.bio: Tidrop is a small sky-blue sea serpent with a rounded head, tiny budding fins on its cheeks, and a short tail that swishes constantly through the air as though it is already swimming. Twin wisps of water-steam curl from its nostrils, leaving tiny droplets wherever it goes. It was found in a thermal pool at the lava crater's edge - the only creature that thrives where boiling water meets molten stone. Trainers say Tidrop's cheerful nature comes from never knowing a cold moment in its life.
stages.note: Tidrop leaves a tiny trail of water-droplets wherever it travels, even in the hottest chambers of the lava crater.

stages.name: Hydrofen
stages.bio: Hydrofen has grown long and sinuous, with a proud crown-like crest of ice-blue spines along its head and a pair of broad webbed wings folded against its sides. Its coiling blue body gleams with frost patterns despite the surrounding heat, and its tail splits into a fan of fin-rays at the tip. It can swim through lava streams by surrounding itself with a shell of pressurized water, emerging on the other side entirely dry. The guardians of the lava crater valued its calm presence - a cold eye in a world of fire.
stages.note: Hydrofen coils around thermal vents at night and absorbs the heat into pressurized water reserves used in battle.

stages.name: Typhdrake
stages.bio: Typhdrake is a massive coiling water dragon with a full crown of sweeping icy-blue horns, enormous bat-like wings edged in silver-blue, and a deep chest armored in overlapping glacial scales. Its body fills the widest corridors of the lava crater, and its passage creates a wall of cold mist that momentarily snuffs the nearest flames. When it speaks, its voice carries the crash of ocean waves against a cliff face. The ancient lore says Typhdrake weeps cold rain whenever a great word is forgotten, and the crater pools refill overnight.
stages.note: Each of Typhdrake's horn-tips holds a frozen drop of ocean water from the day it was born - they never melt.

stages.name: Grimlet
stages.bio: Grimlet is a round dark armadillo whose black-grey armored shell is segmented like stacked rings, and whose red eyes glow faintly in the dim corners it favors. It tucks into Granite Heights' shadowed overhangs, perfectly still, watching every approaching thing with unhurried calculation. It does not run from threats - it rolls into a tight ball, armor interlocking so precisely that nothing can find a gap. Guardians note that Grimlet always knows someone is watching even before the watcher has decided to watch.
stages.note: Grimlet's shell-segments seal together so completely when rolled that even water cannot penetrate - researchers have tested this in streams.

stages.name: Magrum
stages.bio: Magrum is built low and wide - its armored body has expanded into thick overlapping dark plates with faint red seams, and wisps of dark shadow-smoke curl off its flanks. Its snout is flat and heavy, its red eyes now burning brighter. In Granite Heights it occupies the areas where rock overhangs and deep gullies create permanent shadow, and it moves through these with unexpected ease, its broad low profile fitting every gap. It is one of the few creatures that Abalont's agents have never managed to drive from its territory - it simply ignores them.
stages.note: Magrum's shadow-smoke is denser on its left side than its right - no one has found out why, but it has been true in every specimen observed.

stages.name: Infermagrim
stages.bio: Infermagrim is a fortress that breathes. Its body is an architecture of massive black rock-plates layered in overlapping rows, each one shot through with deep crimson lines like cooling magma, and dark shadow-smoke pours from between the seams of every plate constantly. Its face is almost entirely obscured by forward-angled plate-armor, and its eyes are slits of red in the dark. Granite Heights' older guardian records call it the mountain's immune system - the thing the stone sends out when it decides something does not belong. It cannot be pushed. It cannot be lured. It simply arrives, and waits.
stages.note: The plates on Infermagrim's back have never been seen separating - not even during documented battles. It may have permanently fused them.

stages.name: Malykit
stages.bio: Malykit stands upright on two powerful legs with wide clawed feet and long clawed arms raised to its sides - ready for anything from the moment it wakes. Its deep crimson-dark body is lean and angular, with glowing red eyes set in a flat spiky-headed face. It haunts Ghost Hollow's darker recesses, moving with sharp sudden bursts between long stillnesses, and has a habit of scratching territorial marks into trees at exactly eye height for a standing child. Guardians say it watches the guardians' old drills from the shadows and gets visibly agitated when a step is done wrong.
stages.note: Malykit leaves claw marks in trees at exactly the same height every time - never an inch higher, never lower.

stages.name: Malyxen
stages.bio: Malyxen has grown taller and more defined - a lean bipedal imp-lizard with a broad chest and long serrated claws on hands and feet. Its skin is deep purple-red, traced with darker markings, and its glowing yellow eyes carry an intensity of focus. It patrols Ghost Hollow's middle levels with deliberate authority, stopping at each marked territory-point and adding a fresh scratch before moving on. When it fights it moves in sharp angular bursts - no wasted motion, no unnecessary flourish. Guardians say Malyxen is the most efficient creature in the Hollow.
stages.note: Malyxen's claw-marks are catalogued by Ghost Hollow researchers - they form a precise territorial map updated every three days.

stages.name: Malyxord
stages.bio: Malyxord is Ghost Hollow's apex dark creature - tall and broad-shouldered, its body dense and powerful, every surface covered in overlapping dark armored scales that shine like obsidian. Long serrated claws curve at both hands and feet, and its wide chest bears a pattern of deeper crimson lines that pulse faintly. It stands at the Hollow's deepest interior boundary and nothing crosses without its decision. Ancient guardian writings describe Malyxord as the Hollow's last defense - the creature the darkness itself shaped to push back anything that would unmake the world further. Even Abalont's agents keep to the outer ring when Malyxord is present.
stages.note: Malyxord's presence causes every ghost-light in a fifty-meter radius to burn steadier - as if the lights are trying to impress it.

stages.name: Melvit
stages.bio: Melvit is a compact little beast with a bold black-and-cream face pattern and tiny beady eyes that gleam red in firelight. Its stubby body is built like a rounded wedge, short legs splayed wide for digging. It snuffles around the lava crater's cooled edges, nosing through volcanic rubble. Despite its small size, Melvit shows no fear - it will stare down creatures three times its height without blinking. The guardians say Melvit was the first creature to approach the crater willingly, and the volcano didn't dare argue.
stages.note: Melvit has never been observed retreating from anything - researchers have placed obstacles in its path and watched it push straight through every one.

stages.name: Melvix
stages.bio: Melvix has broadened into a powerful, low-slung fighter. Its cream-and-black face now carries a permanent scowl that only deepens when challenged. Its claws leave scorch marks in cooled lava when it walks, and the undersides of its paws radiate heat as if the crater's fire has soaked into the bone. Melvix digs tunnels through solidified lava tubes the way other creatures run through mud - fast and without hesitation. Anything that disturbs one of its tunnels hears about it immediately and at length.
stages.note: Melvix's claw-scratch marks in lava rock glow faintly orange for up to three hours - the heat runs that deep.

stages.name: Melvorax
stages.bio: Melvorax is the undisputed apex of the lava crater - a massive, dark-furred badger-form whose body is laced with glowing lava-red seams running from jaw to tail. Its eyes are solid ember-orange, and when it opens its jaws the inside glows as if coals are burning in its throat. Nothing in the crater challenges a Melvorax, not even the lava itself, which seems to flow around it respectfully. Old crater legends say Melvorax was the one who drove Abalont's fire-shadows out of the deepest tunnels by being more frightening than they were.
stages.note: The ground within ten metres of a resting Melvorax stays warm enough to heat water - hot springs near the crater form where it sleeps.

stages.name: Miaskit
stages.bio: Miaskit is a pale blue-white armadillo-form with articulated bony plates that clank softly when it rolls. Its round eyes are almost too large for its head, adapted to the shadow caves' utter darkness. A faint spectral shimmer traces the edges of each plate, as if the ghost element is seeping out through the cracks in the earth-armour. It rolls into a perfect sphere when startled, and the ball glows like a faint lantern in the dark - confusing predators who expected it to vanish.
stages.note: When Miaskit rolls into a ball, it glows bright enough to read by for exactly forty-three seconds before fading.

stages.name: Miasmole
stages.bio: Miasmole has grown into a heavier, more angular form. Its segmented plates have darkened to slate-blue-grey and carry a faint ghost-light glow at the seams. It moves through the shadow caves with the unhurried confidence of a creature that can walk through solid rock if it chooses to - which it occasionally does, passing half of its body through a cave wall before pulling back out to look confused at itself. Its claws are built for tunneling and leave glowing scratch-trails behind.
stages.note: Miasmole's glowing claw-trails persist on cave rock for up to an hour - shadow-cave explorers follow them as makeshift trail-markers.

stages.name: Miasmorph
stages.bio: Miasmorph barely seems to be fully present - its body ripples at the edges, plates phasing partly in and out of the cave rock, trailing wisps of blue-white ghost-light. It is the oldest thing in the shadow caves, and the caves themselves seem shaped around it, as if the tunnels were carved by its presence rather than by water. Its breath produces a low mist that settles into curling shapes before dissolving - the shadow-cave scholars have been copying them for decades and believe the shapes form a complete map.
stages.note: Miasmorph's mist-breath shapes cycle through the same sequence every forty-seven breaths - scholars call it the 'shadow round'.

stages.name: Chrysmote
stages.bio: Chrysmote is a segmented purple-lavender larva with a single huge round eye at its head-end that gives it a slightly unsettling quality for something so small. It rolls slowly through the valley's leaf-litter, leaving faintly luminous slime-trails that catch moonlight. Unlike other larvae, it is semi-transparent - hold it to the light and the dark outline of the creature inside can be seen stirring. Valley children dare each other to pick one up, and those who do say it makes a gentle singing vibration in the palm.
stages.note: Chrysmote's slime-trail glows for precisely one hour after it passes - night-travelers use fresh trails to tell if the valley is safe.

stages.name: Cocospire
stages.bio: Cocospire is a pointed, leaf-veined cocoon hanging from a valley branch on a single thread of iridescent silk. A pale skull-pattern marks its surface - the ghost element showing through. It sways even in still air. Those who press an ear close say they hear a slow rhythmic pulse from inside, like a heartbeat made of whispers. Guardians believe this is the stage where the creature memorizes every voice it has heard - building a memory in the dark before it opens its eyes to the world again.
stages.note: Cocospire's pulse is audible from 30 centimetres on silent nights - naturalists count it at exactly 18 beats per minute.

stages.name: Morphyx
stages.bio: Morphyx is breathtaking and unsettling in equal measure - a large spectral moth with tattered purple wings edged in glowing pale patterns, and a body that seems slightly out of phase with the world. Its two long antennae trail behind it like ribbons of smoke. It drifts above the valley at midnight, and the glow of its wings is the only light in the deepest shadows. Guardians say Morphyx carries the voices of the valley's sleeping words, releasing them one by one each night so they can be found in the morning.
stages.note: After Morphyx passes overhead, unfamiliar patterns have been reported appearing in dew on leaves - picked out by the morning light.

stages.name: Morlid
stages.bio: Morlid is a rounded, bright-green little fish with wide innocent eyes and a tiny fan-tail. It drifts between coral formations in the bay's shallows, nosing into crevices and blowing small bubbles that carry a faint bitter smell - a warning the poison element is already active, though harmless at this stage. Its big eyes make it look perpetually surprised, and it opens and closes its small mouth even when not eating, as if practicing words it's heard echoing through the water from above.
stages.note: Morlid's bubbles smell faintly of sea-herbs - the bay folk use them to locate schools by sniffing the tide.

stages.name: Morsaur
stages.bio: The baby-faced cuteness is entirely gone. Morsaur is a sleek, muscular green fish with a wide fang-lined jaw and fins that have grown angular and threatening. Its eyes have narrowed and turned sharp. It circles coral formations with tight, fast loops, tasting the current for anything interesting. Its poison sacs have matured enough to cloud a small tide pool, and curious children are reminded firmly to watch from the dock. Despite its fierce appearance, coral-bay keepers note it never bites without being provoked.
stages.note: Morsaur can detect a single drop of blood in the water from 200 metres - bay lifeguards post warning flags whenever one is sighted.

stages.name: Morsalyx
stages.bio: Morsalyx is the undisputed apex predator of the coral bay's middle depths. Its body is a mass of jagged scales and exposed fangs, the jaw disturbingly wide for its body length. Teal-green with darker stripes, it moves with the slow certainty of a creature that fears nothing in the bay. Its poison is now potent enough to discolour the water around it a faint green. Old coral bay fishers say Morsalyx arrived before the bay did - that it is the reason the bay formed, as the sea gathered around it out of respect.
stages.note: Coral growing within two metres of Morsalyx's resting spot is always the healthiest in the bay - the mildly-toxic water keeps parasites away.

stages.name: Sporbin
stages.bio: Sporbin is an adorably round mushroom-cap creature with a pale brown cap and a single glowing blue eye. A soft haze of ghost-energy wisps around its base, faint as morning mist. It bounces through the bug thicket with endearing energy, its cap bobbing with each hop. The ghost element means it occasionally passes partway through a leaf or twig without noticing, then looks startled when it catches what happened. Thicket children follow Sporbin trails because the ghost-haze marks a path through dense undergrowth better than any lantern.
stages.note: Sporbin's ghost-wisps turn green when it is happy and blue-white when it is frightened - a reliable mood-indicator every thicket traveler learns.

stages.name: Fungling
stages.bio: Fungling has grown into a stooped, root-heavy form - broad dark cap, a gnarled woody body with root-like legs dug into the soil, and purple ghost-mist rising steadily from around its trunk. Smaller mushroom growths dot its shoulders. It moves slowly but with deep purpose, and when it stops, the roots extend into the soil and connect directly to the thicket's mycelium network for hours. Fungling seems to hold conversations with the thicket floor, and the purple mist thickens when it is listening to something old.
stages.note: When Fungling's ghost-mist turns deep violet, old thicket explorers start moving quickly in the other direction - they say something ancient is speaking.

stages.name: Arborveil
stages.bio: Arborveil is part fungus, part tree, and part ghost - its massive mushroom cap has grown to shade a full clearing, and its root-trunk body has merged with the soil so completely that it is impossible to say where Arborveil ends and the thicket begins. Ghost-light streams upward through every gap in its cap. It is one of the oldest living things in the bug thicket, and it remembers the guardian order from before Abalont's shadow fell. Arborveil does not move; it grows - imperceptibly, relentlessly, through the dark seasons.
stages.note: Arborveil's cap grows exactly one centimetre in diameter each year - scholars can date the bug thicket's history by measuring its cap rings.

stages.name: Noctix
stages.bio: Noctix is a small round-bodied purple bat with wide glowing eyes and stubby wings it flaps with great determination. A faint violet glow hovers at its chest - the first hint of the heroic energy that runs through its lineage. It roosts in the highest towers of Steel Fortress, dangling upside down from iron beams, and launches itself at any noise in the dark with fearless curiosity. New recruits sometimes mistake it for a piece of equipment until it squeaks and falls on their heads.
stages.note: Noctix always launches itself headfirst toward the loudest noise it can hear, landing on it before looking first.

stages.name: Noctilix
stages.bio: Noctilix stands upright now on powerful clawed legs, its wings spread wide with crackling purple lightning tracing their veins. The glow at its chest has become a constant crackling light, and its eyes carry a focused intensity that makes smaller creatures step aside. It patrols the Steel Fortress ramparts at night, and the guardians learned long ago to leave lanterns unlit when it is on watch - Noctilix reads the dark better than any torch.
stages.note: Noctilix can detect a single unlit candle from 200 metres away purely by the heat it would have made.

stages.name: Noctivex
stages.bio: Noctivex is a great broad-winged bat with two blazing purple rings of heroic energy framing its chest - the sigil that marks it as one of the Steel Fortress's ancient guardians. Its wings, now fully spread, blot out the moon when it circles the Fortress walls on patrol. Those rings pulse with a light that wards off both shadow-threats and doubt. The youngest recruits are told: when you see those twin purple moons moving overhead, the Fortress is safe.
stages.note: The two glowing rings Noctivex carries are said to be promises it made to the first guardian - and it has kept both.

stages.name: Noctkit
stages.bio: Noctkit is a compact dark bat that walks on its wing-knuckles with surprising confidence for its size. Its coat is a near-black grey with a faint purple sheen, and its eyes glow a stubborn bright violet. It was born somewhere in Steel Fortress's lower armory levels and has spent its short life jumping off increasingly tall ledges to test its wings - currently at about the third rung of the ammunition rack. The fortress engineers have quietly started placing cushions.
stages.note: Noctkit has attempted 47 solo flights and landed cleanly on the 48th - it keeps precise count with scratches in the iron pillar it sleeps on.

stages.name: Noctwing
stages.bio: Noctwing has grown broad-shouldered, its wings now wide enough to generate a real downdraft when it hovers, and its eyes carry a serious, guarding energy that unsettles intruders. Its knuckle-walking has given way to confident upright stances, and it patrols the ramparts of Steel Fortress at dusk with the focus of a sentry who has never taken a break. When something unauthorised enters its patrol range, its wings snap open instantly - the sound alone has sent grown adults scrambling back through the gate.
stages.note: Noctwing has memorised every gap, crack, and shadow in its patrol route and can fly it in total darkness without slowing.

stages.name: Noctyvern
stages.bio: Noctyvern (Steel) is a colossal dark bat wreathed in twin blazing purple rings of heroic power - the mark that separates it from all lesser dark-flyers. Its enormous wings carry a weight of centuries, and when it opens them fully inside the Fortress's great hall, every torch gutters as the displaced air rolls through. It does not prowl the walls at night - it IS the night inside those walls, a guardian so old it predates the mortar between most of the stones. The fortress was built around it, not the other way.
stages.note: The twin rings Noctyvern carries have never dimmed - not in 300 years of recorded Fortress logs.

stages.name: Bonelet
stages.bio: Bonelet is a small spider with a round skull-white carapace above a small pale body, six visible legs, and hollow dark eye-sockets that give it the look of a tiny lost ghost wearing spider shoes. It picks its way through Bug Thicket's leaf litter with careful steps, pausing frequently as if it just forgot where it was going. It is not lost - it is simply processing an enormous amount of ghost-echo information from the soil beneath it, which contains centuries of Bug Thicket's layered spirit-history.
stages.note: Bonelet can tell how old a patch of leaf litter is purely by standing on it - it gives a small tremor when the layer beneath is very old.

stages.name: Skelspine
stages.bio: Skelspine is a larger pale arachnid with a spined carapace studded with bony protrusions and a rounder, heavier frame than its predecessor. Its hollow eye-sockets now carry a faint ghost glow, and it has learned to use the spines on its back to anchor itself in the undergrowth and become completely still - practically invisible in the thicket's dappled shadows. It eats ghost-energy that gathers in old insect husks, and is thus very useful to have around anywhere the Thicket's restless past tends to accumulate.
stages.note: Skelspine can hold perfectly motionless for six hours at a time - the record, logged in the Thicket research register, is nine hours and forty minutes.

stages.name: Necrcrawl
stages.bio: Necrcrawl is an enormous pale-white spider with a massive pocked carapace like weathered bone and eight heavy legs that barely make sound as it crosses the Thicket floor. Its body is scarred and ancient, dotted with hollow pits that emit faint ghost-light from whatever it has absorbed over its long centuries in Bug Thicket. It does not spin webs anymore - it simply exists, and the Thicket organizes itself around it with the deference of a forest for its oldest tree. Smaller creatures move out of its path in absolute silence.
stages.note: Necrcrawl has crossed Bug Thicket in the same direction on the same night every year for as long as the oldest records reach - no one has determined where it is going.

stages.name: Pebblet
stages.bio: Pebblet is a compact upright tortoise whose rounded body is covered in rough grey-brown rock-textured skin. A single small green sprout pokes up from the top of its shell like a tiny flag. Its wide eyes and stubby arms give it an endearing look, but the shell already feels like solid granite to the touch. Young Pebblets collect small stones in the crevices of their shells and tumble them around like marbles during play. They are found near the lower trails of the Granite Heights, where the first memory-stones are carved into boulders.
stages.note: Pebblet polishes its single sprout every morning by rolling in the dew-wet grass at the cliff's base.

stages.name: Stonox
stages.bio: Stonox walks on four thick boulder-like legs, its back now a broad plate of segmented rock tiles overgrown with moss and a small leafy plant sprouting from the center. The shell's edges are cracked and layered like a geology sample, each layer a different shade of brown and grey. It moves slowly but with total certainty across the steep granite paths, pausing to press its nose against carved memory-stones and study them. Stonox is so heavy that its footprints become permanent indentations in softer stone - younger creatures follow these prints as trail markers.
stages.note: Every place Stonox has rested for more than a week, a new ring of grass grows in a perfect circle around its shell.

stages.name: Terravian
stages.bio: Terravian is a walking mountain fortress. Its shell has become an enormous segmented dome of stacked granite slabs, each slab carved naturally with mineral veins. A full tree - trunk, branches, and rustling leaves - grows from the shell's crown, sheltering smaller creatures in its canopy. Its four legs are as thick as pillars, and each step sends a faint tremor through the stone beneath. Terravian has stood at the summit of Granite Heights longer than any map remembers, and the guardians say it holds the roots of the whole mountain in place with its stillness.
stages.note: The tree growing from Terravian's shell has never once lost a leaf, even through the fiercest mountain winters.

stages.name: Flarcub
stages.bio: Flarcub stands on four clawed legs with an armored red-and-black body plated in overlapping scales like a knight's armor. A tuft of bright orange fire blazes at the tip of its tail, and its eyes are wide and golden. Even at this young stage its scale plates are fully formed, giving it the look of a miniature warrior. It runs along sand dune crests at dusk, leaving tiny claw marks and scorch spots where its flame-tail sweeps too close. Explorers who camp near the sand dunes often wake to find a Flarcub has singed the edges of their tents while inspecting the campfire.
stages.note: Flarcub can hold a single ember in its closed claws for up to six hours without burning itself.

stages.name: Pyrdrake
stages.bio: Pyrdrake has grown into a fierce four-legged drake with a heavily armored red-black body and a broad, flat-skulled head crowned with spiky frills. The flame at its tail has expanded into a roaring blaze. Its claws are wider and sharper, and the scale plates on its chest and shoulders have fused into a nearly impenetrable breastplate. It hunts alone across the sand dunes, using the shimmer of heat above the sand to hide its silhouette. When it stops moving, it looks exactly like a red-streaked dune rock - only the steady flicker of its tail flame gives it away.
stages.note: Pyrdrake buries itself in hot sand up to its neck each midday to supercharge its flame, then erupts out in a shower of sparks.

stages.name: Infernolith
stages.bio: Infernolith looms over the sand dunes on four pillar-like legs, its body a fortress of black-edged crimson scale-armor. The flame crown blazes from the nape of its neck, and its broad head is flanked by swept-back horns and a chest so wide it blocks out the horizon when it turns broadside. Three separate flame plumes burn from its back like living torches. Its footsteps melt a thin glass layer into the sand. The desert clans say Infernolith was born from the first volcanic vent that burst through the sand dunes and has burned without rest ever since, guarding the dunes from those who would put out every last fire.
stages.note: The glass prints Infernolith leaves in the sand contain tiny trapped air bubbles - each one is shaped like a mark from the ancient fire-sigils.

stages.name: Pinqulet
stages.bio: Pinqulet is a tiny pink-bodied sea creature that curves and bounces through Coral Bay's shallows like a living toy. Its round belly and upturned snout are a soft bubblegum pink, and its cheerful blue eyes are huge and round. A small dorsal fin and a pair of side fins are all it needs to zip around the coral gardens. It has already discovered that staring at the coral polyps causes them to briefly glow pink - an accidental psychic pulse it triggers whenever it blinks at a new creature. Young reef-tenders keep Pinqulets as companions because they alert the bay when storm-waters are coming by spinning in circles.
stages.note: Pinqulet spins left-clockwise when rain is an hour away, and right-clockwise when it's ten minutes away.

stages.name: Pinquale
stages.bio: Pinquale has grown into a sleek, confident swimmer - its body still blush pink but now streamlined, with a longer snout and a confident tail fluke. The side fins have broadened to help it cruise at speed through the bay's deeper channels. Its wide eyes see through murky coral-bay waters as clearly as glass, a psychic sharpening that lets it notice things other creatures miss entirely. It leaps from the water in low arcs at dawn, the spray catching the morning light and scattering it in brief rainbows that the bay's guardian markers track. Pinquale is said to remember every voice raised in its presence, even those whispered under the water.
stages.note: Pinquale's wake always curves in the shape of the last word it heard spoken above the water's surface.

stages.name: Pinquarch
stages.bio: Pinquarch is a magnificent full-grown sea creature whose pink body is now adorned with a glowing golden halo that hovers above its head. Pink feather-like fins trail from its back and flanks, shimmering with iridescent patterns as it glides. Its golden tail-fluke sweeps water into gentle spirals that glow faintly where they touch the coral. The bay's oldest records describe Pinquarch as a living tide-reader - it knows when Abalont's shadow touches the water before any storm appears, and its halo dims as warning. Children who touch its flank claim they briefly understand every language spoken by the sea.
stages.note: When Pinquarch's golden halo turns copper-orange at sunset, the bay clams all close their shells simultaneously.

stages.name: Plumling
stages.bio: Plumling is a tiny round fluffball of soft pink feathers with two enormous round eyes that take up most of its face. A small yellow beak peeks out from the fluff, and its stubby wings are barely visible under all the downy plumage. It lives in the lowest spire crannies of the Dragon Spire, puffed up against the wind. When the spire's updrafts kick in at dawn, Plumling tucks its wings in and lets itself tumble upward like a pink dandelion seed - shrieking happily the whole way. Dragon Spire climbers carry Plumlings in their pockets because the little owlets sneeze out a burst of warm air that rekindles frost-bitten fingers.
stages.note: A Plumling sneezes precisely twelve times every hour - and the thirteenth sneeze always smells faintly of lightning.

stages.name: Plumwing
stages.bio: Plumwing stands upright on two taloned feet, its pink-and-gold feathers now arranged in neat layered tufts. Ear-tufts have grown from the top of its head like small horns, and its amber-gold eyes are sharp and focused. The wings have filled out into broad, capable fans edged with flight feathers. It perches on the Dragon Spire's mid-level ledges and watches the skies for hours, rotating its head nearly all the way around when something catches its interest. When Plumwing opens its wings fully and catches a spire updraft, it can sail upward for half a minute without a single wingbeat, eyes fixed on some distant point only it can see.
stages.note: Plumwing can identify any word spoken in the wind from half a mile away, rotating one ear-tuft toward the sound like an antenna.

stages.name: Plumarch
stages.bio: Plumarch is a magnificent wing-spread owl creature whose pink-and-gold plumage blazes with bioluminescent patterns in full flight. Its wings are enormous, each primary feather edged with a warm golden glow that illuminates the spire's fog. The ear-tufts have grown long and swept back, giving it a crowned look, and its golden eyes see through both dark and storm. It is the Dragon Spire's living lantern - explorers lost in the high crags need only look for the moving glow of a Plumarch's wings to find their way back to the paths. The guardians say Plumarch is the only creature that has ever sat on the spire's highest point and looked across all four regions at once.
stages.note: The glow of Plumarch's wing-edges brightens whenever a name it has never heard is spoken in the spire's ancient guardian language.

stages.name: Pluvling
stages.bio: Pluvling is an endearing small axolotl with a round white-lavender body and a frill of purple-blue feathery gill-fans spread wide around its head. Four tiny legs and a flat tail help it waddle along the poison marsh's shallower edges. Its large eyes are pale and attentive, taking in everything. The gill-fans pulse gently with a faint psychic glow when it concentrates, which it does often - usually while staring at reflections in the water. Despite living in the poison marsh, its own body stays pristine because a thin psychic field filters out all marsh toxins before they reach its skin. The marsh's other creatures leave it alone, recognizing that aura.
stages.note: Pluvling's gill-fans change from purple to blue whenever it detects a lie being told within five meters of the water.

stages.name: Pluvian
stages.bio: Pluvian's body has grown longer and more graceful, its pale lavender-white sides patterned with subtle blue-purple striping. The feathery gill-fans are now wider and more elaborate, flowing back along its neck in sweeping fronds. Four stronger legs let it move easily between water and damp marsh-earth. It moves with an unhurried patience through the poison marsh, using its psychic senses to map the currents flowing under the surface. Pluvian leaves faint glowing trails in the marsh water behind it - marsh-keepers say these trails last six hours and mark safe passage routes through the toxic waterways.
stages.note: The glowing trail a Pluvian leaves in marsh water can be followed safely for exactly six hours before fading - not a minute more.

stages.name: Pluvarch
stages.bio: Pluvarch is a beautiful and alien presence in the poison marsh - its long axolotl body is covered in intricate purple-and-white feather-fin fronds that fan out all along its back and sides, each tipped with a soft glow. Its four legs are elegant and sure-footed on both land and shallow water. Pale psychic light radiates from its entire body, pushing the marsh's toxic haze back in a gentle sphere around it. It rarely speaks, but when it does, its voice carries across the whole marsh as a clear crystalline vibration that resolves into meaning rather than sound. The guardians of the poison marsh believe Pluvarch knows the true name of everything in the marsh, and that saying those names aloud could purify the entire region.
stages.note: A Pluvarch that has lived thirty years will have turned every toxic plant within a ten-meter radius into a medicine herb.

stages.name: Embroot
stages.bio: Embroot is a round orange-red bulb sitting on a ring of dark volcanic rocks, with a crown of flaming orange petals-and-tendrils erupting from its top like a sunburst. It cannot move its body but it can rotate its flame-petal crown in a slow full circle, which it does whenever it senses something interesting approaching. The lava crater's youngest guides learn direction from Embroot clusters - the flame-petals always lean slightly toward the nearest active vent, no matter which way the surface wind blows.
stages.note: Embroot petals always point toward the nearest underground lava flow, even through fifty meters of solid rock.

stages.name: Lavamaw
stages.bio: Lavamaw has unfurled into a taller volcanic creature, its orange-red body now mounted on a rocky base and sprouting several long lava-tendril arms that wave and reach independently of each other. Each tendril glows at its tip and can probe the rock for heat or cracks. In the crater's mid-zone, Lavamaw tendrils sometimes grow up through rock fissures and surprise travelers who step on what looks like solid ground. The guardians use Lavamaw's fissure-sense to map the safest walking routes through the crater's unstable surface.
stages.note: Lavamaw extends its longest tendril in the direction of structural weakness, so miners follow its reach before striking with a pick.

stages.name: Infernoflora
stages.bio: Infernoflora has become a broad volcanic cone-creature sitting on a wide platform of hardened lava rocks, its multiple tendril-arms extended outward like the roots of a great fire-tree, each one thick as a beam. Its interior glows visibly through cracks in its rocky outer shell, and when it contracts its arms the lava inside pulses brighter. In the lava crater it is the anchor - the one creature that never moves, never needs to. The crater's entire ecology orbits it; even the youngest Embroot clusters lean toward it before they lean toward the vents.
stages.note: Infernoflora produces a low sub-frequency hum once every twelve hours; every living thing in a hundred-meter radius pauses for exactly three seconds.

stages.name: Embole
stages.bio: Embole is a compact round creature covered in overlapping lava-rock plates, dark brown with vivid orange cracks between every scale where inner heat glows. It hugs the ground at all times, stubby legs barely visible beneath its heavy shell, and rolls slowly across the granite heights with a sound like a bag of warm rocks. Despite looking completely armored, it is shy and tucks its head into its shell at any sudden noise. The granite heights' miners consider Embole a good-luck sign - finding one near a dig site means the rock face is warm and stable.
stages.note: Embole's shell-plates shift slightly every dawn, expanding as it warms, producing a faint tick-tick sound granite-heights children call the morning clock.

stages.name: Magmole
stages.bio: Magmole has grown into a proper pangolin-lizard with a spine-ridge of upright armor plates running from neck to tail-tip, and its lava-crack glow has intensified to a near-continuous orange shimmer across its sides. Four sturdy clawed legs carry it with surprising speed along the granite ridges, and it can dig through rock faces that would blunt a pickaxe in a single hour. The guardians discovered that Magmole tunnels always run true-north without any instrument - the creature uses the granite heights' geothermal gradient as a compass.
stages.note: Magmole's claws glow brightest just before it strikes rock, as though calling heat forward to soften the stone ahead.

stages.name: Infernole
stages.bio: Infernole is a massive low-slung armored beast, broad as a boulder and covered in thick volcanic plating that blazes with orange-lava cracks from head to tail. Its weight alone cracks the granite underfoot, and each step leaves a warm impression in the rock. When it lowers its head and charges the resulting tremor registers in the granite heights' crystal-monitors half a mountain away. Ancient tunnels in the heights were made by Infernole ancestors, and the current generation uses those same tunnels, slowly widening them year by year.
stages.note: Infernole's underside is cooler than its top; the stone it rests on stays warm for three days after it moves on.

stages.name: Smolsnek
stages.bio: Smolsnek is a small, round-headed orange-brown serpent with a tiny flame flickering at the end of its tail, which it curls protectively inward when resting. Its eyes are large and bright, and it sways in a slow S-curve when alert - a habit that desert traders find either charming or unsettling depending on their experience with fire serpents. It lives in the warm pockets between amber desert rock formations, coiling into tight spirals to sleep. Children who encounter one are surprised by how soft its scales feel, which is not a feature it appreciates being commented on.
stages.note: Smolsnek's flame tail never flickers in wind but always flickers when it is being watched, as though showing off.

stages.name: Inferno
stages.bio: Inferno is a substantial orange-yellow serpent with a row of fire-spines and pointed frills erupting along the ridge of its body. It moves in long smooth waves that cross the desert floor faster than they appear, and the fire-frills glow brighter when it accelerates. In the amber desert it follows the subterranean heat channels beneath the surface, surfacing at points where the sand is hottest. Ancient maps mark these surfacing spots as landmarks - an Inferno will always appear at the same spot within two days of a desert sandstorm.
stages.note: Inferno's spine-frills each heat to a different temperature, and the total pattern of hot and cool frills is unique to every individual.

stages.name: Infernoviper
stages.category: Dragon Serpent of the Amber Waste
stages.bio: Infernoviper is a legendary desert serpent so large its full body can circle a small oasis when it coils. Dramatic fire-wings of living flame fan from its mid-section, and its tail blazes with a permanent torch-flame that serves as a beacon for lost desert travelers. When it rises above the dune horizon the surrounding sand vitrifies into amber glass in a ring beneath it. The guardians of the amber desert believe Infernoviper is the desert's own memory - that it has witnessed every sandstorm, every voice raised in the waste, since the desert was formed.
stages.note: Infernoviper's flame-wings never flap but they change orientation to indicate wind direction; desert pilots have used them as an instrument for generations.

stages.name: Pyrule
stages.bio: Pyrule is a small purple lizard hatchling with a row of orange flame-spines along its back and a thick tail it swings for balance. Its round amber eyes look slightly too large for its face, giving it a perpetually surprised expression it does not feel. It lives in the lava crater's outer cooling-stone zone, hopping between warm boulders and testing each new surface with its tongue before stepping on it. The guardians say Pyrule always picks the next word to learn by touching it with its snout - an instinct no one has fully explained.
stages.note: Pyrule's flame-spines each grow exactly one millimeter per week; its age can be measured by counting the spine-rows precisely.

stages.name: Pyrusaur
stages.bio: Pyrusaur stands bipedal now, its heavy purple body balanced on thick haunches and a long flame-tipped tail. Its flame-spines have grown dramatically, blazing orange from the nape of its neck to its tail-ridge, and its clawed hands glow warm. In the lava crater it runs along the inner lava-lip with surprising grace, using its tail as a counterbalance when it leans to look at the molten surface below. The guardians use Pyrusaur's spine-glow as a temperature gauge - the brighter the spines, the closer the underlying magma.
stages.note: Pyrusaur never puts both feet on the same rock at once; it always keeps one foot ready to push off in a new direction.

stages.name: Pyrusaurex
stages.bio: Pyrusaurex is a dark-purple bipedal dragon of tremendous build, its back blazing with a full ridge of towering flame-spines that form a crown of fire visible from the crater rim. Its tail is as long as its body and burns continuously at the tip, and each footfall shakes the cooled lava crust. The crater's most dangerous inner approaches are its territory - places where the rock surface is thin and no one else dares walk. It was the guardians' companion during the first crossing of the crater's center, and the path it walked is the only safe route still used today.
stages.note: Pyrusaurex's flame-spine crown changes from orange to deep white just before any volcanic event, giving thirty minutes of warning.

stages.name: Crowkin
stages.bio: Crowkin is a dark, fluffy crow chick with sooty blue-black feathers and round red eyes that glow like coals. Wisps of dark smoke curl from its wingtips even at rest. It lives near the entrance passages of the Shadow Caves, hopping through narrow crevices and pecking at crystallized darkness that clings to the walls. Its presence in the caves is ancient - the guardians found carvings of Crowkins in the oldest tunnel walls, suggesting these small birds have nested here since before Abalont's shadow first fell. It is startling but not hostile, and the smoke it trails smells faintly of charred wood.
stages.note: Crowkin's smoke trail persists for several minutes after it has gone, marking its path like a living map through the cave tunnels.

stages.name: Malraven
stages.bio: Malraven has stretched into a lean, long-legged bird like a dark heron, with ragged trailing feathers at the wing-tips and a long curved beak. Its plumage is deep black-blue and its red eyes are brighter now. It picks its way through shallow cave pools with slow, deliberate steps, hunting the shadow-fish that swim in lightless water. Wispy tendrils of dark energy drift from its tail feathers. Guardians who venture into the caves' middle passages say Malraven always appears first - as if checking whether a traveler is worth the deeper paths. It is a gatekeeper that never speaks its terms.
stages.note: Malraven stands perfectly still for up to twenty minutes in shallow water, not hunting - just listening to the dark.

stages.name: Vexwing
stages.bio: Vexwing fills the cave ceiling when it spreads its wings - a massive dark raptor whose plumage bleeds into deep red at the wingtips, the color of cinders cooling in the dark. Its body crackles with dark energy that trails in streamers behind every wingbeat. When it lands in the deep caverns, the temperature drops and every light dims for a moment. It was here before the Shadow Caves had a name; some say it IS the shadow the caves are named for. But the guardians know it chooses its companions carefully - it has carried more than one lost child to the cave exit on its back, silently, in the deep dark.
stages.note: Once Vexwing decides a child deserves safety, it will cross the entire cave system in a single wingbeat to deliver them to light.

stages.name: Scalion
stages.bio: Scalion is a tiny silver-grey pangolin-like creature at its first stage, with a single oversized disc-scale on its head like a helmet visor and a curling tail. One bright blue eye peeks out from beneath the disc with intense curiosity. It moves cautiously but precisely through the Steel Fortress, using the disc on its head to deflect any debris that falls, and its curling tail to anchor itself in narrow passages. Guardians say every child who first enters the fortress sees a Scalion sitting near the gate - and that the Scalion always seems to recognize the ones who are going to make it.
stages.note: Scalion's head-disc is already harder than tempered steel at birth - the fortress smiths tested one and broke three of their best tools on it.

stages.name: Platynox
stages.bio: Platynox has grown into a proper scaled lizard with a broad flat head and a body covered in overlapping steel-bright plates. Its single blue eye is alert and intelligent. It moves low and fast through the Fortress corridors, scouting ahead of whatever guardian it has chosen to follow that day. Its plates are not just armor - when Platynox is excited about a word it has just learned, the plates shift and reflect light in a rippling pattern that veteran trainers can read like a language. It is, they say, the most honest creature in the Fortress because it literally shows its feelings.
stages.note: Platynox's plate-ripple pattern is different for every creature it meets - trainers have documented over two hundred distinct ripples.

stages.name: Aerodactox
stages.bio: Aerodactox stands upright, a gleaming armored lizard-knight with a spiraling tail, plated limbs, and the brilliant blue eye now blazing with accumulated intelligence. Its body is a fortress in itself - layered metal-bright scales over powerful muscle, built for both speed and impact. It guards the Steel Fortress's memory-vault with absolute dedication, and the memories it has gathered over its long life fill its armor like light fills glass. Forged-tough and loyal as the guardians themselves, it believes courage is built one word at a time - and it has been watching to see which children are building it seriously.
stages.note: Aerodactox has memorized every voice ever raised within the Fortress walls - it can quote any conversation from any point in its lifetime, perfectly.

stages.name: Scaup
stages.bio: Scaup is a small, vividly purple chameleon-type creature with big round golden eyes and a coiled tail it wraps around branches like a corkscrew. Its body is covered in small raised scales that gleam with a faint toxic sheen. It moves along the lower stems of the Poison Marsh's plants with precise, measured steps - never rushing, always watching. The yellow eyes seem to process information much faster than anything its small body suggests; it has been seen solving two separate problems simultaneously, one with each eye, while holding perfectly still. It is strange, small, and deeply observant.
stages.note: Scaup solves two separate visual problems at once by directing each eye independently - one tracks prey, the other watches for threats.

stages.name: Scaldor
stages.bio: Scaldor has grown longer and more imposing, its purple scales now deeper and faintly iridescent, its coiling tail wide and powerful. The toxic sheen on its scales is now clearly visible as a faint slick, and it uses this to mark the boundaries of its territory in the Poison Marsh - any creature that follows Scaldor's scent trail without invitation will regret it. It has developed partial camouflage that works especially well in the marsh's purple-tinged shadow-water, where it rests half-submerged, only the golden eyes visible. Those eyes never blink.
stages.note: Scaldor has maintained the same ten-meter territorial boundary markers for three years without variation - it refreshes them every forty-eight hours exactly.

stages.name: Scalerath
stages.bio: Scalerath is a magnificent and dangerous creature - a deep purple dragon-chameleon, its body now muscular and armored with great fin-like back-spines and a magnificent spiraling tail. Its golden eyes burn with intelligence, and the toxic aura it radiates has turned the water in a ten-meter radius around its resting pool a permanently iridescent purple. It is the apex guardian of the Poison Marsh, the creature that other venomous things treat as law. Abalont tried to co-opt the marsh by poisoning its water-songs; Scalerath swallowed each one, neutralized the shadow-toxin, and exhaled the clean word back into the air.
stages.note: Scalerath is immune to every poison found in its region - it identifies new toxins by tasting them once and has never been affected twice.

stages.name: Scorbyte
stages.bio: Scorbyte is a compact orange-brown crab-like bug with one outsized pincer that it holds raised, showing it off at every opportunity. Heat shimmers around it at midday because its shell absorbs sunlight and stores it as warmth in the Bug Thicket canopy. It will grab a hot ember from a campfire with its big claw and carry it around - not to harm anyone, just to feel the heat in its grip. Young Scorbyte are sometimes spotted standing in beams of sunlight with eyes closed, soaking warmth like a tiny sunbather.
stages.note: A Scorbyte's big claw runs consistently warmer than its body - you can cook a small bug-berry against it in under two minutes.

stages.name: Scorpaw
stages.bio: Scorpaw has armored itself in overlapping burnt-orange plates that act as heat vents, letting steam escape between each layer. Its claws are now dual and enormous - one for grip, one for smashing - and the fire trapped inside them turns the striking surfaces cherry-red during combat. It marks its territory in Bug Thicket by scorching claw-prints into the bark of large trees at head height, and those marks never fade. Other bugs avoid its grove unless invited.
stages.note: Scorpaw's striking claw reaches surface temperatures high enough to leave a clear brand in oak bark with a single tap.

stages.name: Infernacle
stages.bio: Infernacle is a massive brick-red armored crab covered in interlocked spikes that radiate heat like a forge. Every plate is thick as a roof tile and carries a faint ember-glow in its grooves. When it fully opens its claws, waves of heat ripple outward in visible bands, and nearby dry brush begins to smolder within five seconds. It walks slowly, since anything that hurries nearby catches fire, and Bug Thicket keeps a wide charred ring around wherever Infernacle has chosen to rest that season.
stages.note: The charred ring around an Infernacle's resting spot grows by roughly one metre per week; old rings can be up to forty metres wide.

stages.name: Scorkit
stages.bio: Scorkit is a small dark-red quadruped dragon with two rounded wing-buds folded tight against its back and a blunt horn-ridge above its brow. Its scales are rough like dried lava and warm to the touch even on the coldest Dragon Spire mornings. It is perpetually curious and tends to follow larger creatures at a distance, watching what they do before attempting it itself. The first thing most Scorkits learn to do is scratch sparks from the spire's flint outcrops with one claw - a small act, but one that clearly delights them.
stages.note: Scorkit's wing-buds, though too small to fly, already vibrate at altitude - locals use this as a signal that a spire wind-shift is coming.

stages.name: Scormaw
stages.bio: Scormaw has grown fully into its dark red scales and bat wings now spread wide enough to catch the updrafts that rise along Dragon Spire's cliffs. Its horns have multiplied across its brow in a low crown, and its tail whips in slow arcs when it perches. Fire comes easily now - a short exhale produces a sustained ribbon of flame that it uses to warm its resting ledge before settling. The spire's older dragons tolerate Scormaw on their ridges, which is considered a mark of real promise.
stages.note: Scormaw's wingbeats smell distinctly of warm sulfur - spire guides use the scent to know when one is circling above cloud cover.

stages.name: Inferscor
stages.bio: Inferscor is a full great dragon - dark burgundy scales that have hardened to the consistency of forge-cooled iron, wide bat wings that block the sun when it soars between spire peaks. Its multiple brow horns sweep back like a crown, and its eyes burn with sustained flame. Each exhale is a controlled column of fire it can hold or release at will, and when it chooses to roar, the sound rolls down from Dragon Spire's summit to the valley below in waves. The guardians' oldest texts describe a creature matching Inferscor as the one who first taught the dragon words of power.
stages.note: Inferscor's fire column can burn for nine continuous seconds before it must pause to breathe - the longest documented sustained flame of any Dragon Spire resident.

stages.name: Scutling
stages.bio: Scutling is a small green isopod - a pill-bug shape with a gently domed back and six stubby legs that carry it in a slow, bobbing walk. It lives in the mossy crevices of Granite Heights' lower ledges where water seeps between rocks, feeding on mineral-rich algae mats. When frightened, it tucks its legs under its body and becomes a smooth pebble-sized lump impossible to distinguish from the rocks around it. The heights' children collect them into small mossy jars, calling them 'living pebbles.'
stages.note: When curled, a Scutling holds its position with a grip equivalent to four times its body weight - trying to pry one open takes real effort.

stages.name: Scutilion
stages.bio: Scutilion has grown flat and wide, its olive-green body now segmented into overlapping plates that slide over each other as it moves - a sound like shuffling stone tiles announces its presence before it is seen. It navigates Granite Heights' steep faces by gripping with all six legs simultaneously, and it prefers to walk along vertical cliff surfaces rather than the flat paths, hugging the rock with each plate of its body making full contact. Its antenna tips brush every crack as it passes, cataloging the mineral content below.
stages.note: Scutilion can travel along a vertical granite face for up to three consecutive hours without rest - it has never been recorded falling.

stages.name: Scutirax
stages.bio: Scutirax is a great golden-tan armored titan, its overlapping body plates now thick as quarried stone and worn smooth by years of cliff-face traversal. Many sturdy legs carry its long broad body with slow hydraulic precision, and its bulk is enough to reshape small rock formations just by pressing through them. Granite Heights' stone-paths are partly formed by Scutirax's regular routes, worn down by centuries of its weight. Guardians say it was here before the first path was carved - the original road-builder of the heights.
stages.note: A well-worn path across Granite Heights was traced back to a Scutirax route - the creature had used it for an estimated 300 years before humans arrived.

stages.name: Scuttlet
stages.bio: Scuttlet is a small brown armadillo with a neatly banded shell and a soft pointed snout it keeps pressed to the sand at all times, reading the ground for vibrations. It lives in the upper dune layer where loose sand shifts constantly, and its banded shell acts as a natural sand-sieve - grains fill the gaps and make it effectively invisible when still. It rolls into a perfect ball at any perceived threat and bounces gently down dune slopes, which appears to be accidental but happens so consistently that researchers now believe it is deliberate.
stages.note: Scuttlet rolled down the same dune 21 times in a single afternoon before researchers realized it was doing it on purpose, not out of fear.

stages.name: Armadex
stages.bio: Armadex has compacted itself into a near-perfect sphere of overlapping grey-stone plates - when curled, it is almost perfectly round, and on the steeper dunes it gains real speed in this form. Uncurled, it stands on four solid legs with a wide rounded body and moves with careful, deliberate steps. Its shell plates have taken on a stone-grey color now that it has grown past the lighter brown of youth, and each band is separated by a visible dark groove. Dune merchants mark territorial boundaries using Armadex's roll-tracks - the lines are always perfectly straight.
stages.note: Armadex's rolled form achieves a near-perfect sphere within 0.4 seconds of curling - faster than the eye can track.

stages.name: Thanatusk
stages.bio: Thanatusk stands wide and solid, its grey stone-plate body bearing a thick spiked tail it drags behind it in the sand - the trail it leaves looks like a plow has gone through. Its large claws press deep footprints into packed dune rock, and when it shakes its body, the plates clatter against each other like a rockslide in miniature. The Sand Dunes' oldest trading routes follow paths Thanatusk has walked for generations - its weight compacts the sand into something firm enough to drive a cart over. The guardians called it the Road-Maker.
stages.note: Thanatusk's tail-spike drag creates furrows up to 30 centimetres deep in packed dune sand - some are used as irrigation channels by dune farmers.

stages.name: Scythlet
stages.bio: Scythlet is a small dark-furred quadruped whose back is already bristling with short metal spikes, hard to the touch and cold even in summer. It lives in Shadow Caves' narrow passages where it can brush both walls at once, using the spikes to feel vibrations in the stone. Its eyes are adapted to complete darkness and reflect a faint silver in lamplight. It is wary but not aggressive, retreating at raised voices - the caves echo strangely and it treats every reverberation as a potential threat. Young ones tap their spikes against cave walls to communicate across the dark.
stages.note: Scythlet can transmit information to others of its kind by tapping its spikes in specific rhythms against shared cave walls - cave researchers call it 'spike-talk.'

stages.name: Scythorn
stages.bio: Scythorn has grown heavy and broad, its coat dark as charcoal and its back spikes now long enough to scrape the cave ceilings. Each spike is individually sharp and has a slight backward curve, making them effective at catching anything that tries to grab it from above. It moves through Shadow Caves with a slow commanding authority, and the smaller creatures part before it without being told. When two Scythorn cross paths in a narrow tunnel, they compare spike-length by standing side by side for exactly thirty seconds before one yields the passage.
stages.note: Scythorn's spike tips are self-sharpening - the points regrow within 48 hours after being broken, slightly sharper than before.

stages.name: Scythorax
stages.bio: Scythorax is a massive dark predator whose entire back and shoulders carry a forest of long steel spikes that rattle softly when it walks - a sound that carries through Shadow Caves' tunnels like a warning bell. Its coat is pure black, absorbing all light, and its eyes glow silver in the deepest dark. The spikes are long enough that Scythorax must turn sideways to fit through certain cave passages, and over centuries it has widened all of its regular routes to suit itself. The guardians' records note that Scythorax spikes were found embedded in the cave walls at heights that suggest it was fighting something immense - a story no one has fully told.
stages.note: Scythorax's regular cave-routes are identifiable by parallel scratch-marks at shoulder height on both walls, left by its outer spike-tips for centuries.

stages.name: Seedasprite
stages.bio: A tiny round face peeks out from a ruff of five broad green leaves arranged like a starfish, with two bright red eyes glowing at the centre. Seedasprite drifts through the Light Grove at ankle height, spinning slowly as its leaves catch the breeze to sense thoughts floating on the air. Each leaf flickers when it catches a name it has never heard drifting from a child's mind. The guardians first spotted it orbiting the grove's oldest song-tree like a slow green planet.
stages.note: Spin a Seedasprite gently and it will echo back the last word you were thinking.

stages.name: Seedaunt
stages.bio: Seedaunt has grown into a wide sunburst of layered leaves edged in gold, with a brilliant ruby gem set at its heart that pulses with each thought it reads. The leaves fan outward in overlapping rings and glow faintly at their tips when Seedaunt concentrates. It hovers chest-high among the luminous clearings of the Light Grove, reading emotions the way a flower reads sunlight. Trainers who earn its trust say it can project calm feelings like warm afternoon light.
stages.note: The ruby gem at Seedaunt's centre grows brighter whenever a child nearby works out something difficult.

stages.name: Seedaryx
stages.bio: Now as wide as a shield, Seedaryx floats upright with vast interlocking leaf-wings that cast green-gold dappled shadows. Gnarled vine-roots spiral beneath it and a great ruby gem blazes at its core, surrounded by ornate twig-filigree etched over centuries. The Light Grove itself seems to breathe in rhythm with it. Ancient lore says Seedaryx once guided Akilla through the grove by lighting words like lanterns along the path - and it still does, for anyone willing to listen.
stages.note: When Seedaryx meditates, every leaf in the Light Grove turns toward it, as if the whole forest is listening.

stages.name: Sharpup
stages.bio: Sharpup is a chubby little shark with navy-blue and yellow colouring and an oversized grinning jaw it can barely close. Its pectoral fins stick out like stubby wings and its eyes are wide and bright with mischief. It bobs near the surface of Coral Bay stealing shiny pebbles and bits of coral from other creatures' hoards. Trainers describe it as the reef's least-threatening scoundrel - it wants to look fierce but mostly ends up looking pleased with itself.
stages.note: Sharpup cannot resist a shiny object - it will abandon a battle mid-fight if something glints on the seafloor.

stages.name: Sharkaw
stages.bio: Sharkaw is now a full-sized powerful shark with a navy-and-gold body and a jaw lined with rows of sharp teeth it displays freely. Dorsal and pectoral fins cut the water cleanly and its dark eyes carry a calculating gleam. It circles the deeper reef channels of Coral Bay, tolerating no trespassing in its claimed territory. The guardians noted it memorizes the location of every reef creature it encounters - it returns to check on the same spot at the same hour each day, as if keeping attendance.
stages.note: Sharkaw patrols exactly the same route at the same time daily - local divers set their watches by its passing.

stages.name: Abyssjaw
stages.bio: Abyssjaw has grown beyond shark into something closer to a dragon of the deep - massive legs have pushed through its flanks, its jaw has widened to an enormous rend of gold-and-dark teeth, and its yellow eyes burn with predatory intelligence. It moves along the bottom of Coral Bay in a slow prowl, stirring up columns of sand that rise like towers. Ancient charts drawn by the guardians show the entire bay shaped around where Abyssjaw chooses to rest, as though the reef grew to accommodate it.
stages.note: The sand towers Abyssjaw raises as it walks sink back down in exactly the shape of letters - researchers are still decoding them.

stages.name: Finlet
stages.bio: Finlet in the Poison Marsh is a dark blue compact shark that has adapted to the murky shallow waters, its eyes narrowed against the stinging mist. It skims low through the surface film of the marsh, eating the toxic water-skaters that other creatures avoid. Its stubby legs let it haul out onto mud banks where it rests with its mouth open, letting the warm marsh air dry its teeth. Children who know the marsh paths say a Finlet following you means you are on the safe route - it avoids the patches where the ground is not solid.
stages.note: Finlet always avoids the soft mud patches - locals follow its tracks to find the safest marsh paths.

stages.name: Sharyx
stages.bio: Sharyx is a lean powerful shark-form with a low flat profile that lets it slide through the marsh reeds without disturbing them. Its blue scales carry a faint iridescent sheen from the toxic minerals it has absorbed over years in the Poison Marsh. It moves in long gliding bursts, almost never breaking the surface, and arrives at a location before you realise it was tracking you. The guardians marked the channel Sharyx uses as a reliable clean-water indicator - it always keeps to the least-contaminated flow.
stages.note: The channel Sharyx swims stays cleaner than the surrounding marsh - its passage seems to filter the water behind it.

stages.name: Megalodon
stages.bio: Megalodon rises from the deepest fens of the Poison Marsh like a continent of dark fin and jaw. Its enormous blue-dark body has evolved fins as wide as sails and a tail that fans out into sharp trailing points. It moves through the marsh mostly submerged, leaving only a dark ridge of dorsal fin visible above the toxic mist. The poison of the marsh runs through it now - it no longer tolerates any water that is not laced with the same compounds it grew up in. Ancient stories say it once swept the entire marsh clean by swimming a single lap.
stages.note: Megalodon's single lap of the Poison Marsh takes three days - plants grow back differently every time it passes.

stages.name: Skelplet
