stages.bio: Skelplet is the skeleton of a small upright theropod dinosaur with large round amber-glowing eye sockets and tiny forearms that clutch at the air. Its exposed ribs are narrow and its small tail-bones flick nervously. Despite being entirely skeletal, it moves with surprising energy - hopping between the warm volcanic stones of the Dragon Spire and letting heat radiate up through its bones like a radiator. Children encounter it first as a small clattering sound in the dark, followed by those two amber eyes peering around a rock.
stages.note: Skelplet seeks out the warmest spot in any room and sits there for exactly an hour before moving on to the next warmest.

stages.name: Skelptor
stages.bio: Skelptor stands upright on powerful hind legs with the full ribcage and spine of a mid-sized theropod, eye sockets burning with deep amber fire. Its forearms are small but its jaws are substantial, lined with individual bone-teeth that clack impressively when it opens wide. It climbs the Dragon Spire's lava-rock shelves at night, apparently drawn to stored heat, pressing its entire skeleton against warm surfaces like it is recharging. The guardians found old etchings showing Skelptor guarding the Spire's flame-carved memory-stones after Akilla's fall.
stages.note: Skelptor's jaw produces a specific clacking rhythm when it is content - locals transcribed it and found it matches an ancient drum-prayer.

stages.name: Skelphadon
stages.bio: Skelphadon is a magnificent terror - a full-sized skeletal theropod with a sweeping thick tail, a huge armoured skull, and fire burning in both eye sockets that casts orange light across the entire Dragon Spire. Its ribcage has broadened and new bone-plates have grown over the joints, giving it a plated war-armour look. When it opens its jaws, a gust of hot air carries ash from somewhere inside the chest cavity. The guardians say it was already ancient when the Spire was first settled - it has watched every guardian pass through and waited for each one to return.
stages.note: The heat from Skelphadon's eye-fire can be felt three body-lengths away - Dragon Spire nights are always slightly warmer wherever it walks.

stages.name: Solkit
stages.bio: Solkit is a bright golden-yellow rabbit with long upright ears that catch the storm-spire wind and large vivid red eyes that hold the steady warmth of a carried sun. It holds its forepaws together in a ready posture and watches everything with focused attention. At high altitude its golden coat shines noticeably brighter, and travellers on the Storm Spire claim seeing it in the distance helps them find their direction even in cloud. It races the high winds Jack the raven once watched from above, carrying a little sun into every storm it enters.
stages.note: Solkit's ears glow faintly in thick cloud - mountain rescuers in the Storm Spire follow those two amber lights when visibility fails.

stages.name: Solhare
stages.bio: Solhare stands upright on strong hind legs with a muscular build and golden-amber fur that catches the light like polished metal. Its long ears are tipped in bright gold and its red eyes have deepened to a determined gleam. The claws on its forepaws have sharpened and it holds them in a ready fighting stance. It trains in the highest wind-lashed platforms of the Storm Spire, using the resistance of the gale to strengthen its strikes. The guardians wrote that Solhare arrives whenever someone faces something too large for them alone.
stages.note: Solhare always arrives from the upwind direction - storm navigators say you can predict its approach by the way the clouds suddenly part.

stages.name: Solarch
stages.bio: Solarch is a blazing figure - a tall upright golden-armoured hare with a full brilliant mane of golden light trailing behind its ears like a comet tail, one arm raised in a strike pose that burns bright enough to cast shadows behind you. Its entire body radiates steady warm light that cannot be put out. On the Storm Spire summit, Solarch's glow is visible from the valley below as a fixed golden star on the peak - the one light that Abalont's shadow never managed to reach. It carries the memory of every brave word spoken by every child who climbed up after the guardians.
stages.note: The light from Solarch at the summit is listed on storm-spire navigation charts as a permanent landmark - it has not gone out in recorded history.

stages.name: Shadolt
stages.bio: Shadolt is a compact black foal with a short dark-purple mane and tail that lift and drift like smoke when the Lava Crater's heat rises beneath it. Its red eyes glow steadily in the volcanic dark. It trots across the cooled lava flats with surprising nimbleness, occasionally stopping to paw at the ground where heat vents hiss beneath the surface. Children who encounter it say it watches them steadily without blinking for longer than is comfortable, then suddenly trots off - and the direction it goes is always toward the safest path through the crater.
stages.note: Shadolt always trots away toward the safest exit from the Lava Crater - lava-zone guides follow it without question.

stages.name: Nightmane
stages.bio: Nightmane is a powerful black stallion with a full purple-smoke mane that streams fire-edged behind it at full gallop. Its red eyes have deepened to a burning intensity and hooves strike the lava rock with enough force to leave scorched prints. It circles the active crater rim at night, and the violet fire in its mane lights the outer edges of the Lava Crater in a slow purple glow. The guardians recorded that Nightmane's presence near a flame vent increases its output - as if the dark fire in its blood calls to the fire below.
stages.note: Flame vents near Nightmane's patrol path run 30% hotter than equivalent vents elsewhere in the Lava Crater.

stages.name: Phantorvex
stages.bio: Phantorvex is a magnificent terror of the Lava Crater - a great black stallion wreathed entirely in violet-purple flames that pour from its mane, tail, and hooves in long cascading streams. Its eyes blaze with ancient fire and its nostrils trail dark smoke. When it runs the full crater rim, the trail of purple fire it leaves lingers for hours, visible from the valley below as a ring of violet light. The guardians say Phantorvex was present at Abalont's first shadow-fall - it watched from the crater edge, then turned and set every fire-marker in the region burning to warn the others.
stages.note: The fire-ring Phantorvex leaves running the full crater rim lasts six hours - Lava Crater communities use it as a nightly clock.

stages.name: Shadowpup
stages.bio: A chunky charcoal-grey pup with a stocky body, two red glowing eyes, and a little spiked ruff of fur that stands up when it is excited, Shadowpup pads through the dark forest like a small storm cloud. Its red eyes see perfectly in zero light, and it spends most nights chasing shadows it mistakes for playmates. The guardians once called these pups the forest's laughter - small, boisterous, and utterly unafraid of the dark that frightens everyone else.
stages.note: Shadowpup can extinguish a candle flame just by staring at it from two paces away.

stages.name: Specwolf
stages.bio: Specwolf has grown lean and angular, its dark fur now split with a wild spiky mane along its spine and a swept-back crest above its glowing red eyes. Four sturdy legs carry it through the dark forest at silent speed - its paws make no sound even on dry leaves. A faint violet aura pulses around its mane when it is alert. It patrols a fixed territory of roughly fifty trees, and any creature that breaks a promise it has made will find Specwolf sitting in its path.
stages.note: Specwolf's fur absorbs moonlight and releases it slowly over the next day as a faint violet glow.

stages.name: Phantomaw
stages.bio: Phantomaw is all dark mass and controlled fury: a huge wolf with charcoal-black fur, an enormous spined mane, and twin wings of deep violet-blue ghost-flame that unfurl when it howls. Its red eyes are set deep beneath a heavy brow, and two curved tusks jut from its lower jaw. The ground does not quite hold its weight the way it should - it steps as if gravity is a suggestion. In the darkest groves of the dark forest, the guardians placed Phantomaw to hold the boundary Abalont cannot cross.
stages.note: When Phantomaw howls at midnight, every leaf in a hundred-metre circle falls silently to the ground at once.

stages.name: Spiklet
stages.bio: Spiklet is a tight ball of ice-blue crystalline spines radiating in every direction, with two small glinting eyes peeking out from the dense cluster. It rolls along the frost-shattered scree where cold air pools against sun-warmed stone, and every spine is razor-edged and faintly luminous. It cannot move fast, but nothing in the peaks wants to nudge it either. The Guardians of Frozen Peaks once used these little balls as lanterns through the longest winter nights.
stages.note: Spiklet can retract all its spines at once and drop into a snow hollow in under a second when it senses danger.

stages.name: Spiconid
stages.bio: Spiconid has flattened into a wide low body plated in dark grey-blue armour, its spines now longer and arranged in dense overlapping rows along its flanks and back. It moves slowly across the high scree, ploughing a clear furrow through the frost. The spines at its front are slightly longer and angled forward, used to wedge apart stones to reach the frost-algae it eats. Young snow-hares use it as a moving shelter, darting between its spines while Spiconid remains entirely unbothered.
stages.note: A single Spiconid spine, once broken off, regrows to full length in exactly eleven days.

stages.name: Crystallurk
stages.bio: Crystallurk barely fits through most cave mouths in Frozen Peaks: a massive low-slung armoured body bristling with enormous ice-blue spines grown thick as stalactites, packed so densely that its body is almost invisible beneath them. Its eyes are slitted and cold, scanning the ice shelf with patient intelligence. When Abalont's influence tried to freeze the whole range solid, Crystallurk was already there - holding the cold in one place so the rest of the range stayed liveable.
stages.note: Crystallurk's outer spine layer is hollow; on calm nights you can hear the mountain wind whistle through it.

stages.name: Coilbug
stages.bio: Coilbug is a small golden-shelled creature, round as a bun with a spiral shell marking on its back and six stubby legs tucked underneath. Its shell catches every scrap of verdant valley sunlight and sends it back as a warm glow. It moves with slow, rolling determination - always in a straight line until it bumps something, then picks a new direction without any visible frustration. The guardians of verdant valley called it the valley's coin - something small, bright, and worth finding.
stages.note: Coilbug's shell produces a faint golden light at night, just enough to show what's directly beneath it.

stages.name: Hornbeetle
stages.bio: Hornbeetle has grown into a proper large beetle with a gleaming gold-amber carapace, six strong legs, and a single curved horn rising from its head. The spiral on its shell has been integrated into the carapace plating as a raised ridge. It walks with a low centre of gravity and a swinging, sure-footed gait. It carries dung-ball sized objects for other verdant valley creatures when asked - nobody quite knows why, but it seems to find the work satisfying. Its horn catches morning light and throws a small sunrise onto the grass each dawn.
stages.note: Hornbeetle pushes a perfect sphere of golden leaf-pollen wherever it walks, growing larger until it decides to bury it.

stages.name: Spirolith
stages.bio: Spirolith is enormous - a towering golden armoured beetle standing upright on four thick legs with two powerful forelimbs held forward. Its carapace is engraved with deep spiral runic patterns that pulse with warm light when it takes a slow breath. A massive curved horn crowns its head. It anchors itself at the centre of verdant valley during solstices, and every creature in the valley instinctively gathers near it - not out of fear but because its golden light makes unfamiliar names feel possible.
stages.note: When Spirolith beats its wings - once a year, at midsummer - the entire valley hears a single deep resonant chime that lasts thirty seconds.

stages.name: Spirling
stages.bio: Spirling is a plump purple caterpillar with spiral markings along its entire body, each segment ringed in a swirling circle that pulses faintly with psychic light. It moves in a slow, deliberate S-curve rather than a straight line, as though writing something with its path. Every leaf it passes on the verdant valley floor is turned face-up by a gentle unseen force. It is so calm and slow that other creatures often step over it without noticing, which suits Spirling perfectly - it is in no hurry.
stages.note: Spirling leaves a faint invisible psychic trail that keeps the precise shape of its path for up to six hours.

stages.name: Cocolix
stages.bio: Cocolix is a large purple egg-shaped cocoon decorated with deep spiral swirls that faintly rotate in one direction when observed. It rests perfectly still in the verdant valley, balanced on nothing visible. Inside, something is reorganising - the spirals on its shell slowly shift position over days, and children who sit near it and speak find their thoughts come out clearer. The guardians say Cocolix is the moment between knowing a word and truly understanding it.
stages.note: No one has ever seen a Cocolix fall over - even in high wind, even placed on a steep slope, it simply stays put.

stages.name: Spiralyx
stages.bio: Spiralyx emerges as a wide-winged purple butterfly with broad wings printed in deep spiral eye-patterns and soft curved edges. Its large vivid eyes hold a calm psychic glow. It drifts through verdant valley on slow wingbeats, and wherever it passes, the air shimmers faintly with an after-image of its wing pattern. Children in the valley say if you watch Spiralyx long enough and then close your eyes, you will remember the hardest word you ever learned - perfectly.
stages.note: Spiralyx's wingbeats produce a low psychic frequency that is below hearing but causes nearby flowers to open slightly wider.

stages.name: Spotmew
stages.bio: Spotmew is a small spotted green-and-tan kitten with round luminous eyes, a compact body, and a short tail. Its spots are olive-dark on a bright grass-green coat, and two tiny raised scale ridges run along its back - just the beginning of something armoured. It was born on the cooler outer slopes of the lava crater, where the heat from below makes the grass grow tall and unusually tough. It plays in the grass verges, pouncing on lava beetles and carrying them three steps before letting them go.
stages.note: Spotmew's spots are slightly warm to the touch - warmer on the left side than the right, for reasons no one has confirmed.

stages.name: Spottyx
stages.bio: Spottyx is a stocky, powerful ocelot with dark olive spots on a vivid grass-green coat and a full row of raised scale ridges running from neck to tail-base. Its amber eyes are fixed and confident. The scale ridges are hard enough to deflect small lava-rock chips when the crater vents suddenly. It claims territory on the middle crater slopes where grass and rock meet, patrolling a loop of about 200 paces every morning and evening without variation. Lava crater creatures that threaten the grass slopes quickly learn to avoid its ridge.
stages.note: Spottyx sharpens its ridge scales on cooled lava rock each morning; the grooves it carves have been measured growing half a centimetre deeper per year.

stages.name: Spottyrax
stages.bio: Spottyrax is a large, long-bodied champion with a heavy ridge of overlapping dark-gold scales running its full length, a broad chest, and four powerful legs. Its deep olive-green coat is patterned in bold spots that seem to absorb rather than reflect lava glow. The scale ridge can spread slightly when it is challenged, flaring like a defensive crest. It stands at the point where the lava crater's fire meets the surrounding grassland - and the grass on its side has never burned, not once, in living memory.
stages.note: Spottyrax has not changed its territory boundary by a single metre in over twenty years - the exact line is known to every lava crater creature.

stages.name: Spynlet
stages.bio: Spynlet is a tiny purple sea slug moving through shadow caves on a slow muscular foot, its soft rounded body dotted with small pale spots and topped with two short sensory antennae-horns. Its colour glows faintly with toxic warning - nothing in the shadow caves eats it, which suits it perfectly. It leaves a thin luminescent trail of psychic slime that persists for hours, and small shadow insects have been observed following these trails to navigate the darkest passages.
stages.note: Spynlet's trail glows strongest at the exact spot where it paused longest - always where the air is warmest.

stages.name: Spynose
stages.bio: Spynose has grown to the length of a forearm and developed a dramatic ridge of sharp golden-tipped spines running down its back in alternating rows. Its body is vivid purple with pale yellow spots scattered across the softer flanks. The spines carry a mild contact venom, but Spynose only raises them when crowded - otherwise they lie flat. It navigates shadow caves with remarkable accuracy despite the dark, reading the psychic imprints left in cave walls by everything that has ever touched them.
stages.note: Spynose has been observed pressing its antennae to cave walls for up to twenty minutes - researchers believe it is reading old impressions.

stages.name: Spynarch
stages.bio: Spynarch is a wide, heavy-bodied sea slug filling the shadow cave floor from wall to wall when it fully extends. Its back is a forest of long, stiff violet-purple spines that spread sideways and catch the faint cave glow. The spots on its flanks have grown into iridescent eyes-patterns that seem to follow you. It moves at the pace of a slowly turning page, but covers ground steadily. The shadow caves' most venomous passages are also Spynarch's territory - other creatures navigate around its route, not through it.
stages.note: Spynarch has mapped every shadow cave passage in living memory - it corrects its own path by a fraction of a degree to explore a new section every single year.

stages.name: Spykling
stages.bio: Spykling is a small, dark-crimson dragon-bat with a wide head, two large red eyes, a stocky body, and stubby wings it cannot yet use for sustained flight. Its feet are large and clawed for clinging to the lava crater's vertical walls, which it does for most of the day, watching everything below with unblinking red eyes. In short glides it launches itself from ledge to ledge, and each landing is precise. The other crater creatures do not push it off its ledge - it seems too certain for something so small.
stages.note: Spykling licks the cooling lava rim each morning - researchers believe it is reading the temperature to decide when to move.

stages.name: Spyxon
stages.bio: Spyxon has grown bipedal and humanoid in outline - a lean, tall dark-crimson drake standing upright on two muscular legs with two broad arms ending in claws, and wide leathery wings folded at its back. Its red eyes glow in the lava crater's thermal haze. It can launch itself from the crater rim and circle the entire crater in a single thermal, riding the heat without a wingbeat. It does not chase things. It waits and glides, and arrives exactly when expected.
stages.note: Spyxon's shadow is consistently thirty centimetres longer than its body size should produce - no one has found an explanation.

stages.name: Spyxalor
stages.bio: Spyxalor is a fully grown dragon with the proportions of a warlord - massive chest, broad wings that shadow a ten-metre circle when spread, a long heavy tail, and enormous clawed forelimbs that grip the lava crater rim with casual ease. Its deep crimson scales have darkened toward black at the wing joints, and its red eyes hold a low burning glow. It is old enough to remember when the lava crater was formed, and the guardians placed it there not as a threat but as a recorder - its body heat has mapped every eruption for a century.
stages.note: Spyxalor exhales a smoke ring once each hour, on the hour - no one has ever observed it miss.

stages.name: Pebshell
stages.bio: Pebshell is a small round tortoise with a smooth grey-brown domed shell marked by a single small blue gemstone embedded in the top. Its four stubby legs shuffle slowly through the Amber Desert's hot sand, and it blinks with a look of calm concentration that makes it seem older than it is. The blue gem is thought to be a piece of ancient amber desert crystal it absorbed at hatching. Pebshell sleeps buried to its shell-rim in warm sand and emerges only when the temperature drops at dusk.
stages.note: Pebshell can stay buried in sand for up to four days without surfacing, surviving entirely on stored warmth.

stages.name: Rockarmor
stages.bio: Rockarmor is a stocky, broad-shouldered tortoise whose shell has roughened into a thick layered carapace of grey and amber stone. Its face has settled into a permanent squint - whether from the desert glare or deep thought, nobody is certain. When it plants its feet and sets its shell flat, even strong winds rolling across the desert floor can't budge it. Caravans have learned to camp in the wind shadow of a resting Rockarmor, which seems unbothered by company as long as nobody touches its shell.
stages.note: The grooves in Rockarmor's shell map perfectly to the ridge patterns found in the oldest amber rock formations of the desert.

stages.name: Crystallyx
stages.bio: Crystallyx carries an eruption of pale ice-blue crystal spikes across its back like a mountain range, each spike as long as a grown person is tall. Its shell has become geological - thick as a fortress wall, with visible mineral strata running through it. Despite its mass, it moves with deliberate calm, each footstep leaving a crater in the desert floor. The crystals on its back are said to have taken five hundred years to form, and they ring like bells when the desert wind passes through them at exactly the right angle.
stages.note: When desert winds hit the crystals at the right angle just before dawn, the sound carries for thirty kilometers.

stages.name: Pebblyx
stages.bio: Pebblyx is a compact little round creature of sandy brown with a single teal crystal spike growing from its forehead like a proud antenna. Two large blue eyes give it an expression of perpetual wonder, and it scampers through the Crystal Mines' lowest tunnels poking its nose into every glittering crack. The crystal on its head is sensitive - it hums faintly near rich ore veins, making Pebblyx an accidental treasure-finder that miners quietly follow through the tunnels without letting on.
stages.note: A Pebblyx's crystal hums at exactly the pitch of the ore vein it senses - higher for crystal, lower for raw stone.

stages.name: Cragyx
stages.bio: Cragyx has developed a broad armored body studded with multiple sharp rock spikes across its back and head, with two thick forward-facing horns flanking its face. Its hide is a mottled grey-brown, textured like natural stone, and it moves surprisingly quickly through the mine corridors with a low, wide-legged gait. When threatened it lowers its head and presents the full array of spikes in a flat defensive shield. Crystal Mines workers leave offerings of smooth pebbles at Cragyx's favorite resting spots - insults taken otherwise.
stages.note: Cragyx can reverse direction instantaneously without slowing - miners still argue over how its legs accomplish this.

stages.name: Cragolith
stages.bio: Cragolith stands like a jagged peak given legs, its body wrapped in dense overlapping stone plates and its head crowned with a jagged ring of pale crystal spikes. The crystal crown is not decorative - it channels seismic vibration from the mine walls directly into its skull, giving Cragolith awareness of every movement within three hundred meters. It communicates with other Cragolith through low-frequency pulses that travel through the stone itself, imperceptible to any creature without rock in its bones. The mines feel quieter when a Cragolith is watching.
stages.note: Cragolith can pinpoint a single footstep through forty meters of solid crystal mine wall using only vibration sense.

stages.name: Strixlet
stages.bio: Strixlet is a small, fluffy grey-white owl-like bird with a rounded face, two white feather tufts on its head, and fierce bright eyes far too intense for something so soft-looking. It nests in the lower crevices of Dragon Spire where updrafts provide lift for its short practice glides. Though it cannot yet sustain flight against the spire's full wind, it spreads its stubby wings and tilts into every passing gust as if daring the wind to knock it over. The dragon-riders of the region consider Strixlet sightings a good omen.
stages.note: Strixlet is known to stare into lantern flames for up to two hours at a time - blinking only once per minute.

stages.name: Strixion
stages.bio: Strixion has developed a full coat of spiky grey feathers that fan outward around its face like a ruff, giving it a much wider, more imposing silhouette. Its eyes have deepened in color and its talons are now strong enough to grip Dragon Spire's sheer rock faces in winds that would strip a person off the ledge. It hunts at the shoulder of the spire where the thermals converge, turning its wide-faced gaze on anything that moves below. The feathers around its face are so fine they detect air pressure changes a moment before the gust arrives.
stages.note: Strixion always turns to face incoming wind exactly 1.5 seconds before anyone or anything else on the spire notices the gust.

stages.name: Strixigon
stages.bio: At its final form, Strixigon of the Dragon Spire has become wholly dark - its feathers are deep black-blue from wingtip to tail, and its spread wings fill the sky like a moving stormfront. Its face retains the wide owl shape, but the expression has shifted from fierce to ancient - a creature that has witnessed the full arc of Dragon Spire's history and found it worth watching still. The dragons of the spire give Strixigon distance; there is a shared understanding between them that neither will explain. Its call at night sends a chill through the whole region.
stages.note: Even the oldest dragons of the Dragon Spire stop and hold still when Strixigon calls at night.

stages.name: Tortlet
stages.bio: Tortlet stands on two legs, clutching a smaller detached shell-disc in one stubby fist like a shield or a toy it found very interesting. Its main shell is a warm sandy-brown dome across its back, and its face is set in the focused expression of a creature already measuring everything for eventual combat potential. It practices blocking moves with its shell-disc on anything it encounters in the Amber Desert - rocks, cacti, other Shellmites - and has never once been observed sitting still longer than a minute.
stages.note: Tortlet has memorized the exact shell-disc throw angle needed to ricochet off three desert boulders and return to its hand.

stages.name: Terrashell
stages.bio: Terrashell has grown into a broad-shouldered bipedal tortoise-warrior with thick shell plates covering its chest and arms in overlapping layers. Its face has grown fiercer and its posture more deliberately defensive - it stands with its weight shifted forward, always ready to brace. The desert sun has darkened its shell to a deep amber-brown and the wear marks from years of combat practice are clearly visible in the scuffed shell surface. It positions itself at the threshold of any area it considers its own and waits. And waits. And waits.
stages.note: Terrashell has held a single defensive stance in the same desert canyon gap for sixteen days straight - pausing only to eat.

stages.name: Terradon Rex
stages.bio: Terradon Rex is built like a walking fortress - golden-amber shell plates cover every surface of its wide bipedal body in an overlapping architecture that leaves no gap for anything to reach the creature beneath. Its face is broad and stern beneath a heavy shell brow, and it carries itself with the unhurried authority of something that has never once needed to move quickly. Every shell plate is scarred with the marks of past confrontations that ended in Terradon Rex's favor. Amber Desert legends say it is the last line of defense before the desert's oldest ruins - and that nothing has passed it in three hundred years.
stages.note: No single impact in recorded history has cracked any of Terradon Rex's shell plates - the oldest ones are over four centuries old.

stages.name: Thornmite
stages.bio: A small, vividly crimson-red fox-puppy with a bushy tail and bright red eyes, Thornmite darts through the Dragon Spire's lower shadow-corridors in swift zigzag bursts that confuse the eye. Its fur is a deep blood-red with slightly darker patches, and its ears are oversized and radar-alert. Despite the ominous region, Thornmite is curious and bouncy - it has a habit of snatching small shiny objects and caching them in crevices. The Dragon Spire's records note that Thornmite tracks are found near every treasure cache, great and small, in the whole spire.
stages.note: Thornmite caches stolen items in exactly seven separate spots and rotates between them, never returning to the same spot twice in a row.

stages.name: Thornpede
stages.bio: Thornpede has grown into a lean, long-legged wolf with fur the colour of deep arterial red, its back ridge now lined with sharp dark spine-quills that stand when threatened. It moves in long silent strides across the Dragon Spire's midnight levels, always slightly ahead of where the light reaches. Multiple tails swish behind it in a fluid motion - it is unclear from a glance how many there are. Thornpede hunts alone, uses shadows as cover with an almost tactical intelligence, and has memorised every guard rotation in the Spire.
stages.note: Thornpede can flatten its spine-quills so completely that it passes through a crack half its apparent width - experienced hunters still do not know how.

stages.name: Infernathorn
stages.bio: Infernathorn is unmistakable - a massive crimson-furred beast with nine distinct dark-tipped tails fanning behind it like a living crown of shadow, and a broad scarred face that holds the quiet menace of something that has never needed to rush. Its spine-ridges have become full blade-quills, and its red coat darkens to near-black at the extremities. The Dragon Spire's eldest guardian text says Infernathorn appeared before the first dragon took residence, and it permitted the dragons to stay - not the other way around.
stages.note: Each of Infernathorn's nine tails is said to hold the memory of a defeated rival - it has never grown a tenth.

stages.name: Mudhorn
stages.bio: A round, powder-blue dragon-hatchling with a cream-coloured belly disc, stubby horn nubs, and an expression of permanent cheerful bewilderment, Mudhorn sits near the Lava Crater's cooler rim pools and blows small mud-bubbles with its nose. Its little forearms are stubby and expressive, and it slaps the muddy rim with them when excited. Despite the volcano's danger, Mudhorn is entirely unbothered - it has found a warm mud-puddle beside a cooling lava shelf and considers this the perfect home. Guardian lore says Mudhorn was the first creature to figure out that lava cools into useful rock, and has been sitting nearby feeling proud ever since.
stages.note: Mudhorn blows exactly one bubble at a time and waits for it to pop before blowing another - it has never been seen to blow two at once.

stages.name: Thormud
stages.bio: Thormud is a compact upright dragon brute, dark navy-blue with a broad tan belly and rows of stubby earth-brown dorsal spines running up its back. Its arms are thick now, its posture solid and square, and its horn nubs have grown into proper curved points. It lurches between crater pools with heavy bipedal steps, scooping cooling lava-mud to pack onto its spines - apparently for temperature regulation, though it looks like it is simply proud of being messy. Its deep rumbling vocalizations echo off the crater walls at all hours.
stages.note: Thormud re-packs mud onto its own spines approximately every ninety minutes - researchers have timed this to within five minutes without exception.

stages.name: Magmamoth
stages.bio: Magmamoth is a titan of the Lava Crater - jet-black hide that has absorbed centuries of volcanic heat, a broad spiked back of dark volcanic rock-points, and a belly still carrying the tan-warm colour of cooling lava. Red-orange ember eyes glow steadily in the crater smoke. It stands completely still for hours at crater's edge, watching the lava flow, and the crater's regular creatures have learned to sleep near it for warmth and protection. Ancient crater lore says Magmamoth and the volcano struck a bargain: the volcano stays where it is, and Magmamoth stays nearby to keep it company.
stages.note: Magmamoth's body temperature has been recorded at 58 degrees Celsius at the surface - it runs ten degrees hotter than the warmest recorded lava-rim rock.

stages.name: Thorncub
stages.bio: A fluffy, round moss-green bear cub with a single pale leaf-thorn sprouting from the top of its head, Thorncub toddles around the Dragon Spire's mossy base levels snuffling at every crevice. Its vivid green coat catches the Spire's filtered light and makes it look like a walking bush - an effect Thorncub seems to use deliberately by sitting among ferns when it wants to rest undisturbed. It loves to press its single head-thorn against things to test their hardness, and the thorn is already stronger than it looks. The Spire's older guardians say Thorncub always knows where the hidden exits are.
stages.note: Thorncub's head-thorn test-prods every new surface it encounters - dragon-scale, stone, wood, and guardian boots have all received equal investigation.

stages.name: Thornbear
stages.bio: Thornbear has grown broad and imposing, its mossy-green coat now shot through with red-tipped spine-thorns that stand erect when it is threatened - turning a rumpled bear into a pincushion-obstacle that nothing wants to rush. It moves through the Dragon Spire with a rolling, confident gait, stopping to excavate moss and fungi from rock faces with strong curved claws. Despite looking fierce, Thornbear has a precise, calm quality to its movements - it only raises its thorns when the situation genuinely warrants it. Dragon Spire hatchlings have been documented sleeping against Thornbear's thorned flank, apparently trusting the signal system completely.
stages.note: Thornbear's spines have been documented standing erect a full three seconds before any human-perceptible threat appears - it registers danger earlier than any nearby guardian.

stages.name: Thornothyr
stages.bio: Thornothyr is a great dark-shelled bear-titan whose body has grown so large and still that fungi and lichen colonise the flat surfaces between its massive thorns. Its back is covered in overlapping dark-brown thorn-plates sharp enough to split stone, and its jaw can crush granite. It walks the Dragon Spire's deepest fissures with the unhurried weight of something that has never needed to run. When Thornothyr stands on its rear legs - which it does when truly angry - it blocks the entire passage it is in. Ancient Spire records describe it as the wall between the Spire's fissures and whatever is behind them.
stages.note: Lichen colonies on Thornothyr's back are taxonomically different from any found elsewhere in the Spire - they have only been found growing on this creature.

stages.name: Thornchick
stages.bio: A tiny bipedal wyvern hatchling with a dusty olive-green body, a single blunt party-hat horn on its head, and a round green spot on its chest like a leaf-badge, Thornchick totters around the Dark Forest floor squawking at falling leaves. Its little forearms are nearly vestigial and it balances with a comically intense expression. The horn is harmless for now but grows with remarkable speed - forest elders have measured a Thornchick's horn extending three millimetres in a single day. Dark Forest saplings grow faster in the patches where Thornchick sleeps, apparently benefiting from something it exhales at night.
stages.note: Saplings in a five-metre radius of a Thornchick's sleeping spot grow measurably faster than those outside it - the mechanism is not understood.

stages.name: Thornwing
stages.bio: Thornwing has grown into an elegant pterosaur-form with broad membranous wings edged in vivid pink-purple veining, and two elegant curved head-crests that sweep back like a compass rose. Its leaf-patterned wings beat in slow arcing circles over the Dark Forest canopy, and the undersides catch forest light to flash the wing-veins in brilliant colour. It rides thermal columns above the treeline and calls downward in spiraling glides, letting the forest guide its path. Dark Forest hunters use Thornwing circling patterns as a map of where air-columns are rising - it reliably marks forest clearings from above.
stages.note: Thornwing circles exactly three times before landing, always completing the third circle even if clearly tired - the pattern never varies.

stages.name: Thornodactyl
stages.bio: Thornodactyl is a formidable wyvern-dragon of the Dark Forest - a great dark-green scaled beast with enormous crystal-pink wing-spines, powerful hind legs, and a body armoured in overlapping scale-plates. Its head bears a full crown-array of crystal-blade horns, and its tail ends in a heavy scythe-tip. When Thornodactyl spreads its full wingspan above the Dark Forest canopy, it creates a brief silence - every bird, bug, and smaller creature holds absolutely still until the shadow passes. Ancient Dark Forest lore says Thornodactyl and the forest struck a peace: it does not burn the canopy, and the canopy shelters its eggs.
stages.note: Dark Forest fires have never spread to the two square kilometres around Thornodactyl's nesting site - investigators found no structural difference in the trees, only the creature's presence.

stages.name: Thornyx
stages.bio: A compact, bright-green lizard-shaped creature entirely covered in layered leaf-spines that make it look like a walking pile of fresh foliage, Thornyx forages across the Bug Thicket floor using its thick spiked tail for balance. Its big round eyes are leaf-green and alert, and its leaf-quills are supple enough to bend around branches without snagging. It sits motionless among actual leaves to vanish entirely - the only tell is the faint curl of its tail tip. Bug Thicket young are taught to count the leaves in a bush carefully before sitting on it, because of Thornyx.
stages.note: Thornyx is camouflaged well enough that three Bug Thicket survey teams failed to spot one sitting on an open path in full daylight.

stages.name: Quillhog
stages.bio: Quillhog has grown into a muscular four-legged lizard with a full spine-mane of earth-tone quills - green at the tips, brown and orange mid-shaft - and a long sweeping tail ringed with spine-clusters. It moves through the Bug Thicket with a low, deliberate prowl, pressing its belly close to the ground when hunting and rising onto stiffened legs when defending. The quills have become properly weaponised now: a full body-shake releases a shower of barbed spine-tips into the air around it. Thicket insects give it a wide berth, which suits Quillhog perfectly.
stages.note: Quillhog's body-shake defense fires spine-tips in a two-metre radius - it can replace its full quill-coat in approximately thirty hours.

stages.name: Fernarch
stages.bio: Fernarch is a great armoured lizard-behemoth whose body has merged with the Bug Thicket itself - its spines have grown so long and tangled with actual living vines that it now carries a full canopy of ferns and small plants on its back as it moves. Its four legs are pillar-thick, and its tread opens furrows in the thicket floor that quickly become waterways. Fernarch moves slowly, eats constantly, and has remodelled more of the Bug Thicket's terrain than any other creature. Ancient thicket records call Fernarch the Gardener-Who-Walks - every major fern-grove in the thicket began as a spine-plant dropped from Fernarch's back.
stages.note: Every major fern-grove in the Bug Thicket has been traced to a location where Fernarch rested; the spines it sheds take root and grow.

stages.name: Sproutnyx
stages.bio: A small, lush-green kitten with oversized tufted ears and a single bright green leaf sprouting straight up from between them, Sproutnyx pads through the Shadow Caves on silent paws, investigating every fungal bloom with its nose. The leaf on its head is mildly toxic to touch but Sproutnyx seems unaware of this, pressing it cheerfully against things for emphasis. It is clever enough to open sealed containers by working at the seams with its paws, and cave foragers have learned not to leave food low to the ground. The Shadow Caves' elder texts describe Sproutnyx as the creature that discovered which cave fungi are edible by eating all of them and surviving.
stages.note: Sproutnyx has consumed seventeen cave fungal species toxic to other creatures without apparent ill effect - researchers are still cataloguing its internal adaptations.

stages.name: Thornlynx
stages.bio: Thornlynx has grown into a long-bodied, muscular lynx with a full coat of overlapping green-and-brown leaf-scales, sweeping leaf-plume tail, and vivid orange-green eyes that glow slightly in the Shadow Caves' darkness. Thin toxic vine-tendrils grow from its spine and trail behind it as it moves, leaving faint chemical trails that other Shadow Cave creatures learn to avoid. It hunts by ambush, pressing its leaf-pattern coat against the cave walls until it is invisible, then striking with extraordinary speed. It has been in the Shadow Caves long enough to have memorised the scent-signature of every creature that shares its territory.
stages.note: Thornlynx's vine-trails remain chemically active on cave rock for up to six hours after it has passed - it effectively keeps a dynamic chemical map of its territory.

stages.name: Venomarch
stages.bio: Venomarch is a terrifying apex presence in the Shadow Caves - a massive red-scaled predator bristling from nose to tail with toxic blade-horns, its back a ridge of venomous spines, its jaw a wide-set weapon capable of crushing stone. The vivid red colouration is not camouflage: it is a warning the Shadow Caves eventually taught everything else to obey. Venomarch secretes a territory-marking toxin from its spine-tips that lingers for days; nothing enters its range without that signal. Ancient Shadow Caves lore says Venomarch was created by Abalont's shadow as a guardian of the deepest passages - and it accepted the role.
stages.note: Venomarch's spine-toxin has been detected in Shadow Cave water samples six hundred metres from any known Venomarch sighting - it marks territory more deeply than any visible boundary.

stages.name: Toxadpole
stages.bio: A round, bright-green toadlet barely bigger than a fist, Toxadpole has wide yellow eyes and two small purple orbs dangling from its sides like toxic baubles. Its belly is a sickly yellow-green, and its stubby limbs end in round, sticky toes. Restless and curious, it hops in tight circles when it senses a name it has never heard - tapping its baubles together to produce a soft, venomous chime. In the Light Grove's glowing clearings, it pokes its nose into every glowing flower, sniffing for the sweeter poisons.
stages.note: Its purple side-orbs glow faintly at dusk, luring night insects straight into its waiting mouth.

stages.name: Toxarump
stages.bio: Standing upright now, Toxarump is a stocky green toad with a muscular chest, scarred knuckles, and a purple-trimmed sash tied around its waist bearing a small skull emblem. Its yellow eyes have grown more slanted and fierce, and thick poison pores line its back and shoulders. It has learned to punch first and ask questions later - the sash catches any venom that drips from its fists. It holds the shadowed edges of the Light Grove like a bouncer who never forgets a face.
stages.note: Trainers who try to sneak past a Toxarump find its fist in the way every single time - it never sleeps on its feet.

stages.name: Toxazaur
stages.bio: Toxazaur is a hulking, war-scarred toad covered in dark blotches and thick ridge-like poison glands along its spine. Its giant fists drip with a violet venom that pools on the ground wherever it stands. The skull emblem on its sash has grown into full spiked shoulder-armor, and its eyes burn yellow with ancient menace. In the Light Grove, it is the shadow beneath the brightest trees - something the guardians noticed only after it had already been watching them for years.
stages.note: A single drop of Toxazaur's dripped venom can keep a patch of ground toxic for seven days straight.

stages.name: Jellotox
stages.bio: Jellotox is a tiny, round-capped jellyfish in purple and pink, bobbing gently with four thin, trailing tentacles that drip a faintly luminous venom. Its face - two wide eyes and a tiny open mouth - gives it a permanently startled expression, as if surprised by its own existence. It drifts through the Ghost Hollow, pulled by breezes no living creature can feel, and its tentacles leave short glowing streaks in the air. It seems to be looking for something it lost long ago.
stages.note: Jellotox produces one tiny venom droplet per hour - if you bottle it, the liquid glows soft purple all night long.

stages.name: Toxjelly
stages.bio: Toxjelly has grown into a wide-capped jellyfish with prominent yellow-green spots across its dome and long, sinuous tentacles hanging below. Its body has a half-real quality - light passes through it at certain angles - and it moves through solid stone walls as readily as through open air. The spots pulse in sequence when it senses danger, broadcasting a warning that other Ghost Hollow spirits heed immediately. Where it drifts, the air tastes metallic and faintly sweet.
stages.note: The yellow-green spots on Toxjelly's cap pulse in a pattern unique to each individual - experienced hollow-guides can tell them apart at a glance.

stages.name: Venomjel
stages.bio: Venomjel spans wide - its domed cap now as broad as a child is tall - and its many long tentacles spiral outward like the arms of a dark galaxy. Purple and deep green swirl across its surface in slow, hypnotic patterns that mimic the night sky above Ghost Hollow. Anything brushing a tentacle feels a profound chill before numbness sets in. Venomjel does not hunt; it simply drifts, and those who linger too near drift along with it, forgetting where they were going.
stages.note: Venomjel has been observed drifting the exact same route through Ghost Hollow for three years - no one knows what it is circling.

stages.name: Tuskbit
stages.bio: Tuskbun's first form is a round, fluffy, light-brown creature - part mole, part digging machine - with two oversized crystalline diamond-blue tusks erupting from its snout that are already bigger than the creature's head. Its tiny round eyes peer out above the tusks with determined calm, and it holds its stubby forelimbs close to its chest. In the Steel Fortress, young Tusklets bore exploratory shafts through walls, leaving perfectly circular tunnels the diameter of their tusks - which architects quietly use as ventilation.
stages.note: A Tuskbit's crystal tusks are harder than most drilling tools used in the Steel Fortress - the garrison tests new chisels against shed tusk-fragments.

stages.name: Tuskburrow
stages.bio: Tuskburrow has grown stocky and low-slung, its fur thicker and brindled, with three massive crystal-blade tusks that jut forward and slightly outward - a drill-head configuration. Its powerful forelimbs end in broad, shovel-shaped paws perfect for clearing debris behind its tusk-cuts. It can chew through packed earth and softstone at a walking pace. The Steel Fortress tunnels it excavates are so geometrically precise that construction crews sometimes request a Tuskburrow before laying water pipes.
stages.note: Tuskburrow always circles a tunnel entrance once counterclockwise before entering - construction teams call this "the twist" and consider it good luck.

stages.name: Burrowtitan
stages.bio: Burrowtitan is a low, wide-bodied hulk whose multiple enormous crystal-blade tusks and back-spines form a complete drilling and breaking array. Its fur has given way to thick, interlocked hide plates that look almost manufactured. The creature moves slowly but with total commitment - no material it has faced has stopped it. In the Steel Fortress it is both worker and warden, digging the deep foundations that keep the great walls standing. It barely notices battles; it simply puts its tusks to the obstacle and pushes.
stages.note: Burrowtitan's largest tusk has survived every recorded impact without cracking - metallurgists believe it has a microstructure no forge can replicate.

stages.name: Burrowlet
stages.bio: Tuskora's first form is a small, dark-purple mole with two gleaming silver crystal-blade tusks proportionally enormous for its body, tiny star-shaped pink ears that rotate independently, and a round velvet snout. Its small forelimbs are already broad-pawed and built for digging. In the Light Grove it burrows up into glowing clearings at dusk, squinting at the brightness before deciding it is worth it, and then diving back down at the slightest loud noise.
stages.note: Burrowlet moles use their star-shaped ears like radar - one full rotation in each direction before they surface anywhere new.

stages.name: Tuskora
stages.bio: Tuskora has grown wide and low, its dark body now thick with muscle and its crystal tusks gleaming silver-blue in any light. Its paws have widened into formidable digging tools edged with hardened steel-like nails. Small red star-shaped markings sit behind its shoulders - possibly sensory organs, possibly ornamental. It spends most of its time just below the surface of the Light Grove, creating a dense network of tunnels that routes moisture to the grove's oldest trees - a fact the trees seem to appreciate.
stages.note: Tuskora digs its tunnel network to within a hand-width of every major tree root in its territory - never breaking through, just staying close.

stages.name: Tuskquake
stages.bio: The Light Grove's Tuskquake form is a wide-bodied, ridge-backed mole-titan whose entire dorsal surface is covered in overlapping armour plates that look forged rather than grown. Its multiple massive crystal-steel tusks radiate outward like a crown of blades. It moves underground mostly, but when it surfaces - which happens only for significant threats - the ground bulges and cracks before it emerges. The grove's oldest guardian trees are said to have grown up around the routes this creature carved, their roots tracing every tunnel like a map.
stages.note: When Tuskquake surfaces in the Light Grove, the surrounding trees lean slightly toward it for three minutes afterward - as if greeting an old friend.

stages.name: Pigmole
stages.bio: Pigmole is a round, golden-brown creature blending pig and mole: a wide snout, small forward eyes, and two tiny crystal-blue tusks flanking its nose. Its stubby body barely clears the ground, and its feet are wide-pawed for digging. In the Granite Heights it burrows into the thin soil between rocks, surfacing to sniff the cold mountain air and immediately going back down. It communicates with other Pigmoles by tapping its tusks against buried stones - a surprisingly complex language made entirely of knocks.
stages.note: Each Pigmole has a personal tusk-tap rhythm - other Pigmoles recognise individuals by the beat alone, even through ten feet of granite.

stages.name: Groundtusk
stages.bio: Groundtusk has emerged as a powerful digging beast with a wide muscular back, heavy shoulders, and strong claws designed to break through compacted granite. It burrows headfirst into solid rock-face with its broad snout acting as a wedge, and its dark coat is permanently streaked with granite dust. Its eyes have grown even smaller as it relies on vibration-sensing through its wide paws to navigate. On the Granite Heights it creates hidden tunnels just wide enough for itself - and precisely that narrow.
stages.note: Groundtusk emerges only at night and seals each tunnel entrance with a plug of earth it mixes with its own saliva - the plugs are waterproof.

stages.name: Terravorn
stages.bio: Terravorn erupts from the ground rather than climbs out of it - a massive, dark, soil-caked behemoth with wide crushing forelimbs, a scarred and heavy snout, and a back that is half-buried by the mountain dirt permanently clinging to its hide. Its tusks are broad and deeply scored. A dark aura clings to it, not evil, but profoundly ancient - the kind of darkness that belongs to deep places where light has never reached. The Granite Heights have recorded this creature's emergence sites for generations: the same three clearings, decade after decade.
stages.note: Terravorn always surfaces at the same three granite clearings, ten years apart - the locals put out a flat stone as a landing pad, and it uses it every time.

stages.name: Umbrapup
stages.bio: This Umbrapup is a small, compact wolf pup with fur so dark it absorbs light, bright yellow eyes that pierce the cave gloom, and small rounded ears that track every sound. Wisps of shadow drift from its paws when it walks, leaving a faint ghostly trail. It follows the old patrol routes of the Shadow Caves instinctively, before any trainer ever teaches it to - as if the paths are already written into its bones. The guardians believe Akilla's loyalty passed into these pups when he was lost to Abalont's shadow.
stages.note: Umbrapup pups always run the same patrol loop when left alone - the exact route varies by individual, but none of them ever learned it.

stages.name: Nightfang
stages.bio: Nightfang is a lean, athletic wolf whose body seems to blur at the edges, as if it is slightly out of phase with the solid world. Shadow wisps trail from its flanks and muzzle constantly, and its glowing yellow eyes are the brightest things in any cave it enters. It runs its patrols at a precise trot - the same speed, the same corners, the same pauses. Any creature that falls into step beside it is safe for as long as they keep pace. The Shadow Caves remember every guardian who ever walked them.
stages.note: Nightfang pauses at the exact spot where old patrol logs say Akilla always stopped to check the eastern passage - every single round.

stages.name: Abysswraith
stages.bio: Abysswraith is barely a body at all - a vast dark wolf-shaped wraith with swirling shadow tendrils instead of solid limbs, glowing yellow eyes visible from forty metres in total darkness, and a howl that shakes dust from cave ceilings. It runs its eternal patrol at full speed now, shadow-tentacles streaming behind it, and any shadow it passes through becomes impassable to Abalont's creatures for a full day. The guardians believe Abysswraith is keeping Akilla's place warm, and that it will step aside the moment he returns.
stages.note: Abysswraith's patrol completes in exactly the same duration every time - to the second - regardless of how many obstacles have changed.

stages.name: Veilkit
stages.bio: Veilkit looks like a smooth, grey-purple oval with two wide, glowing lavender eyes and a single bright psychic gem embedded in its belly. Tiny stubby limbs press close to its sides, and the whole body has a pearly sheen as though lit from inside. It sits perfectly still in shafts of light that filter through the Psychic Temple canopy, soaking up the luminous energy of light-trees. It communicates entirely by pulsing its belly gem - one pulse for yes, two for no - before it has yet grown a voice.
stages.note: Veilkit's belly gem pulses exactly once per second; a double-pulse means it has sensed an unfamiliar sound nearby.

stages.name: Veilsect
stages.bio: Veilsect has encased itself in a segmented purple-grey cocoon of chitin, three horizontal bands of ridged armour wrapping its torso. Its head emerges with large compound eyes glowing violet and a pair of small antennae that quiver to pick up stray thoughts. The gem has moved to a deep recess in its chest and pulses with a slow, rhythmic throb. Resting against light-tree trunks in the Psychic Temple, it absorbs the stored warmth stored in the bark and grows its mind quietly in the dark.
stages.note: Press an ear to a light-tree where Veilsect rests and you will hear faint notes humming back - borrowed sounds it is memorising.

stages.name: Veilstyx
stages.bio: Veilstyx hovers among the highest light-trees of the Psychic Temple, patrolling corridors of still, humming air. The Guardians called it the Keeper of Promises - it remembers every voice it has ever stood near, and forgets none of them.
stages.note: Veilstyx can replay any voice it has ever heard in perfect clarity, projecting it as a shimmering note audible only to the person who first spoke.

name: Veldfawn

stages.name: Veldfawn
stages.bio: Veldfawn is a small golden-green deer fawn whose body is entirely wrapped in layered leaves and soft mossy fur, with bright amber eyes and a tiny cluster of twig-antlers sprouting from its forehead. Its legs are slender and sure-footed, and a fringe of small leaves runs along its back like a mane. It wanders through the Dark Forest's lighter clearings where thin beams of sunlight pierce the canopy, standing perfectly still in each beam to absorb the rare light. The forest creatures nearby grow calm and slightly brighter in its presence.
stages.note: Veldfawn turns its twig-antlers to face the nearest pinprick of sunlight the way a flower tracks the sky.

stages.name: Veldeer
stages.bio: Veldeer has grown tall and slim, with big branch antlers that hold only a few last leaves. Its legs are slowly turning into twisted bark and roots, leaves fall from its body as it walks, and green spirals glow softly on its side. It walks calmly through the forest in autumn, knowing that every ending is also a beginning.
stages.note: Every leaf Veldeer drops sprouts into a new seedling by spring.

stages.name: Sylvanarch
stages.bio: Sylvanarch is the ancient spirit of the dead wood. Its body is made of pale grey-white bark covered in green moss, its huge twisted antlers drip with hanging moss, and its eyes glow bright green. Glowing spirals and cracks shine across its wooden body. It is the guardian of old trees, and where it walks, new life grows from the fallen wood.
stages.note: Sylvanarch can stand so still among the old trees that travelers walk right past it without noticing.

blurb: Veldfawn lost its herd among the glowing trees. Help Veldfawn find its friends!
watch: Watched over by the Guardian Akilla.
facts: Deer can run fast and jump very high.
question: What is a baby deer called?

stages.name: Sproutlet
stages.bio: Sproutlet is a round, freshly-hatched chick still wearing the bottom half of its eggshell like a little skirt, its yellow-green down fluffy and bright. Two small leaf-like wing-nubs sprout from its sides and a neat tuft of green feathers tops its head. Its beak is short and bright orange and it opens wide whenever wind passes through - as if it is tasting the Gale Ridge's famous updrafts for the first time. It follows whatever is moving nearest to it and cheeps loudly when left alone.
stages.note: Sproutlet cannot yet fly but bounces nearly twenty centimetres when it flaps hard enough - the eggshell skirt rattles like a tiny drum.

stages.name: Leafawk
stages.bio: Leafawk is a bright green parrot with a long elegant tail feather, a rounded white-crested head, and wide wings that it holds slightly open at all times as if ready to catch the next gust. Its eyes are large and golden and it tilts its head sharply to listen - it repeats back any sound it hears within three seconds, always perfectly pronounced. At the Gale Ridge it is prized by young learners because it refuses to let a mispronounced sound go unchallenged, chirping the correct form until they get it right.
stages.note: Leafawk will repeat a sound back exactly seventeen times before it gives up - trainers have counted.

stages.name: Verdantyx
stages.bio: Verdantyx is a magnificent green griffin with a broad feline body, powerful feathered wings broad enough to block the sun, and a proud crested head with a fierce golden eye. Its plumage is vivid green and gold, and its primary feathers are as wide as ssounds. When it launches from the Gale Ridge's crags, the downblast flattens every blade of grass in a five-metre circle. The guardians treated it as a living storm-warning: when Verdantyx circles three times instead of two, a full tempest is coming within the hour.
stages.note: Verdantyx circles clockwise in fair weather and counter-clockwise when a storm is forming - Gale Ridge keepers stake their safety on this.

stages.name: Squeamox
stages.bio: Squeamox is a small, round dark brown mouse with enormous amber eyes that take up most of its face, two oversized front teeth, and stubby powerful forepaws built for digging. Its ears are large and round and it holds its hands pressed together in front of its chest as it sits. It burrows into the Sand Dunes with impressive speed - a Squeamox can vanish into dry sand in less than two seconds flat - and it caches food pellets in small side-chambers off its main tunnel, then systematically forgets which chambers they are in.
stages.note: A single Squeamox tunnel system has been found to contain forty-three separate food caches - none of them ever revisited after the initial digging.

stages.name: Gnawmox
stages.bio: Gnawmox is a lean, battle-scarred sand rat with long whiskers, narrow amber eyes, and a long bare tail trailing behind it. Its brown fur has the texture of worn leather and its forepaws have grown heavy and clawed from years of excavation work. It moves low and fast across the Sand Dunes at night, hugging the shadows between dune crests, and rarely appears in the same place twice. Its gnaw-marks on dune stone have been studied and found to contain patterns - whether language, map, or simple habit, no one can yet say.
stages.note: Gnawmox gnaw-marks on dune stones always face north - researchers have proposed several theories and confirmed none of them.

stages.name: Pestilox
stages.bio: Pestilox is a massive, hunched armadillo-rat with a thick plated back of overlapping earth-brown armour scales, a wide flat head, enormous curved claws, and a long thick tail it swings as a club. Its small amber eyes glow dully in the dark of the deep dunes. It has abandoned the surface almost entirely, operating through a network of tunnels beneath the Sand Dunes so extensive that large sections of dune occasionally collapse into them. The Sand Dunes' few surface-dwellers treat the sudden appearance of a Pestilox as a serious warning that the ground ahead is unsafe.
stages.note: A section of Sand Dune that has partially collapsed overhead is almost certainly sitting above a Pestilox tunnel junction - they always collapse at the intersections first.

stages.name: Vespling
stages.bio: Vespling is a small purple-grey bat with round body, stubby pointed wings, and a single bright violet eye at the centre of its face. It does not land - it hovers at all times, rotating slowly on the spot when stationary. It inhabits the Shadow Caves' upper chambers where thin shafts of moonlight occasionally penetrate, and it chases these light beams the way other creatures chase warmth, circling them until they fade. Its ghost-nature means it passes through cave walls with no effort and often reappears on the other side mid-chirp, startling the creatures it was talking to.
stages.note: Vespling passes through solid rock with a faint pop that can be heard up to three metres away - experienced Shadow Cave spelunkers count the pops to track how many are nearby.

stages.name: Vespral
stages.bio: Vespral is a sleek dark purple bat with large leathery wings, long pointed ears, and wide glowing crimson eyes that catch no light source - they make their own. It flies through the Shadow Caves in absolute silence, wings producing no sound at all, which is physically impossible for its wing-loading - the guardians documented it as its ghost nature suppressing the sound of its own movement. It appears in places ahead of where it was last seen with no intermediate flight time observable.
stages.note: In seventeen timed observations, Vespral crossed a thirty-metre cave chamber in under one second - far beyond any biological flight speed.

stages.name: Vestigon
stages.bio: Vestigon is a vast dark creature with enormous black leathery wings, a heavy angular body trailing tendrils of shadow-smoke, and two blazing red eyes that cast reverse shadows - pools of deeper darkness where light should be. It rules the deepest chambers of the Shadow Caves where no natural light has ever penetrated and no map has ever been completed. The guardians recorded it as the thing that decides which memories the Shadow Caves keep and which ones dissolve - and it has been deciding for longer than the caves themselves have had a name.
stages.note: The pool of deeper darkness cast by Vestigon's eyes grows by one square centimetre per year - Shadow Cave keepers measure this annually with quiet reverence.

stages.name: Virkling
stages.bio: Virkling is a plump, bright-eyed green leopard cub with vivid lime-and-grass green fur spotted in bold darker green rosettes. Two small curved ears sit wide on its head and its tail curls up in a cheerful hook. It bounds through the Dark Forest with enormous energy, pouncing on fallen leaves and investigating every mushroom ring it finds. Akilla's forest was its home before the shadow fell, and even now Virkling returns to the old guardian-paths, sniffing the moss for traces of the old protectors. It trusts slowly - but once it does, its loyalty is absolute.
stages.note: Virkling follows every new path in the Dark Forest twice - once to test it, once to memorize it - and never uses the same route twice in a row.

stages.name: Viridaunt
stages.bio: Viridaunt moves with quiet, self-assured grace through the Dark Forest, its emerald leopard coat now full and rich with rounded rosettes. It patrols the boundary between the safe inner forest and the shadow-tainted outer fringes, marking trees with claw-rakes at exactly child-head height as a warning to others. It keeps Akilla's old patrol routes alive through pure habit and memory. Children who pass through its territory and speak honestly find it falling into step beside them - a green guardian for the old paths.
stages.note: Viridaunt claws a fresh mark into a guardian-tree every morning at dawn; foresters who study these marks can predict its daily route with near-perfect accuracy.

stages.name: Virantheon
stages.bio: Virantheon stands upright on powerful haunches, broad-shouldered and commanding, its vivid green body bright even in the deepest Dark Forest shadow. Huge rosette-spots glow with forest energy and its heavy tail sweeps slow and deliberate. Where it walks, the shadow retreats. It carries the memory of every guardian word Akilla ever spoke in this forest, and repeats them in a low rumble at the roots of the oldest trees as though feeding them meaning. Children who earn its trust say it places a single large paw on their shoulder, transferring a warmth that lasts for days.
stages.note: The rosettes on Virantheon's coat rearrange slightly over decades - old illustrations show different patterns, and scholars track the changes like a living constellation map.

stages.name: Viperyx
stages.bio: Viperyx (poison line) is a small, cheerful-looking purple-lilac serpent with a single glowing white horn on its forehead that gives it the air of a tiny, serpentine unicorn. Wide eyes and a broad smiling face make it seem approachable - which is somewhat misleading, as its horn carries a weak numbing charge. It coils in the shallower channels of the Poison Marsh, occasionally rearing up to flash the horn at anything that interests it. New trainers consistently underestimate it. The guardians noted that its horn pulses faster when it hears unfamiliar names, as if trying to record them.
stages.note: Viperyx's horn-glow brightens when it encounters a word it hasn't heard before - marsh guides say the brightness is a reliable measure of how new an experience is.

stages.name: Noxyx
stages.bio: Noxyx rears high in a wide cobra-hood spread, its body now deep blue-purple with banded steel-blue ridges and short back-spines. The single horn has grown prominent and sharp, and a thin venom-mist wisps from its fangs. It holds the deepest lily-channel stretches of the Poison Marsh as territory, and any creature approaching its marker stones receives one warning rattle of back-spines before being driven off. Despite its fierce territory-keeping, Noxyx has been observed using its horn to carefully lift trapped insects from sticky marsh-plants and deposit them on safe lily pads - a quirk that marsh scholars find fascinating.
stages.note: Noxyx uses its horn to draw geometric patterns in the marsh mud each dawn; researchers haven't agreed on whether the patterns are territorial markings or something else entirely.

stages.name: Toxhydra
stages.bio: Toxhydra is massive, its deep blue-grey body coiled into ridged mountains of scale, and its broad hood edged in sharp ice-blue spines that make it look armored even at rest. The single horn has become a great swept ridge of crystalized venom. Poison mists roll continuously from its open jaw. It owns the deepest known chamber of the Poison Marsh, where no other creature dares rest. Ancient accounts describe Toxhydra as the reason the Poison Marsh was never fully claimed by Abalont - not because it opposes the shadow, but because it opposes all intrusion with identical ferocity. The shadow learned not to compete.
stages.note: Toxhydra's shed skin sections have been found up to two kilometres from its territory - researchers believe other creatures carry them as deterrents against predators.

stages.name: Sparkmouse
stages.bio: Sparkmouse (mouse line) is a small, round-eared mammal with tan-brown fur, wide bright eyes, a round belly, and a tiny glowing blue orb floating beside its tail like a personal lantern it never seems to notice. It hops through the Steel Fortress's maintenance catwalks with enormous confidence for its size, investigating every bolt and joint. The blue orb occasionally zaps the metal surfaces near it, leaving faint scorch-marks that workers follow like a trail of evidence to find where Sparkmouse has been. It is impossible not to like - it has the absolute certainty of something that has never been told it shouldn't be wherever it currently is.
stages.note: The floating orb beside Sparkmouse's tail always hovers at the same relative distance regardless of how the creature moves - it has never been dislodged by any force yet attempted.

stages.name: Voltail
stages.bio: Voltail has grown into a stocky, upright draconic form with broad wings folded at its sides, tan-brown scales covering a wide chest, and a face set in permanent serious concentration. Its wings already carry electrical field markings in vivid blue and it stands on strong digitigrade legs. The playful chaos of Sparkmouse has organized into focused power - Voltail patrols assigned sections of the Steel Fortress with the dedication of a guard who takes its role seriously. Junior engineers hand-feed it copper wire, which it accumulates and delivers to forge-workers as apparent gifts.
stages.note: Voltail's wings, even folded, generate enough field to keep the immediate area's instruments running on backup power during a full primary outage.

stages.name: Thunderwing
stages.bio: Thunderwing is an imposing dragon with a heavily muscled frame, vast scaled wings that crackle with persistent lightning along their leading edges, and a broad heavy head set with fierce golden eyes. When it spreads its wings inside the Steel Fortress's main hall, the lights dim and then surge. It has stationed itself near the Fortress's outer gate and treats every creature that passes as personally its responsibility to evaluate - allies receive a short nod, strangers receive the full wing-spread and electric display. It is the Fortress's unofficial gatekeeper and takes no days off.
stages.note: Thunderwing's wing-spread can charge a fully depleted power core in under four minutes - Fortress engineers have documented this and built a failsafe protocol around it.

stages.name: Sparkling
stages.bio: Sparkling is a chubby, wide-faced draconic axolotl with vivid blue scales, small but sturdy limbs, and a yellow mane-crest that crackles with faint static between its spines. Its wide-set round eyes carry a cheerful, unbothered expression. It shuffles through the Steel Fortress's water-cooling channels and drainage troughs, pausing frequently to zap small floating debris with its mane-static and watch it spin. Fortress technicians adore it unconditionally despite its habit of shocking anyone who reaches for it without warning.
stages.note: Sparkling's mane-static recharges fully after a short swim in cold running water - it returns to the coolant channels after every zap like a creature who has found the perfect resource loop.

stages.name: Voltlotl
stages.bio: Voltlotl (axolotl line) has grown into a long-bodied draconic lizard with vivid blue scales, spined back-crest, and powerful four-legged stance. Its mane-crest has matured into full electric spines that arc between tips continuously. It moves fast along the Fortress's wall-rails and overhead struts, scaling them with suction-tipped claws, and has developed a sharp tactical intelligence - it has been observed redirecting power fault-currents away from sensitive equipment by placing itself as a bridge. Engineers credit it with preventing three major Fortress fires.
stages.note: Voltlotl (axolotl line) can climb any metal surface at full running speed - the ceiling included - and has been photographed sleeping upside-down from the Fortress's main archway.

stages.name: Stormlotl
stages.bio: Stormlotl stands at full height as a formidable blue-scaled dragon, four powerful limbs braced wide, electric spines forming a continuous crown along neck and back. Lightning arcs between every spine-tip in a permanent crown of electricity visible across the entire Fortress. Its gaze is sharp and calculating. It controls the Fortress's upper-tier power-routing with apparent intelligence - operators discovered that the most efficient power distribution patterns were not what they had programmed, but what Stormlotl had rerouted. They have since stopped reprogramming and let it run the grid.
stages.note: Stormlotl's spine-crown produces enough ambient charge to power the Fortress's secondary lighting system indefinitely without drawing from the primary grid.

stages.name: Volteel
stages.bio: A slender blue eel no longer than a child's forearm, Volteel bobs upright in warm shallows with two tiny bright antenna-horns quivering on its snout. Its long ribbon tail fans out like a sail to keep it steady in the tidal drift. In Coral Bay's reef gardens, young Volteel hatch in clusters beneath lightning-struck coral formations and immediately begin hunting the tiny sparks that crackle along broken reef edges - learning to call home by following the electric taste of the water.
stages.note: Volteel navigates entirely by electric taste - it flicks its horns like antennae to sample the charge in the current.

stages.name: Amphydra
stages.bio: Amphydra's scales have darkened to deep blue, and its antenna-horns have lengthened into crackling prongs that fork the water ahead of it. A bright electric aura pulses along the full length of its body, and its large round eyes have turned pitch-black, reading the electromagnetic field of every fish within twenty meters. It no longer hunts along the reef - it hunts by waiting at the reef's edge until prey swims into range, then releases a single short discharge.
stages.note: Amphydra's electric pulse is precisely calibrated - enough to stun a reef fish, never strong enough to shatter coral.

stages.name: Thunderwyrm
stages.bio: Thunderwyrm fills the deepest channels of Coral Bay with its presence - a colossal eel with a fanged dragon's jaw that gapes wide enough to swallow a dinghy whole. Lightning arcs and froths in a continuous wreath around its whole body, and the sea glows pale blue for a hundred meters in every direction when it passes. Ancient sailors charted Coral Bay's reefs by the light it cast, calling it the Wandering Beacon. It speaks in electric pulses that the reef creatures translate into warnings and welcomes.
stages.note: The bioluminescent ring around Coral Bay's deepest trench is not coral - it is the resting glow of a sleeping Thunderwyrm.

stages.name: Sparksting
stages.bio: A bright golden scorpion small enough to fit in a cupped hand, Sparksting carries a stinger that glows vivid yellow at its tip and hums like a live wire. Its eight legs pick through the leaf litter of Bug Thicket with meticulous precision, and it taps each twig with a foreleg before stepping on it - checking for stability. In Bug Thicket's layered canopy floor, Sparksting is at the very base of the food chain and knows it, staying under leaves and low cover and only raising its glowing stinger when cornered and frightened.
stages.note: Sparksting taps every surface exactly twice before placing weight on it - trainers call this the Sparksting Double-Check.

stages.name: Voltscorp
stages.bio: Voltscorp has deepened to tawny brown with electric arcs sparking between its claw joints, and its tail has curved into a tighter coil at the tip where the charge concentrates. It holds its pincers wide and low, threatening but patient - it will wait an entire hour in perfect stillness for the right moment to strike. In Bug Thicket it claims territory by scorching a ring of thin electric traces into the bark of nearby trees. The other insects respect these borders absolutely.
stages.note: A ring of thin black scorch lines on tree bark at ground level means Voltscorp has claimed everything inside the ring as its territory.

stages.name: Thunderstinger
stages.bio: Thunderstinger is colossal by Bug Thicket's standards - its golden body radiates a continuous electric field that makes every other insect nearby orbit it at a respectful distance. Lightning arcs span the full length of its body from claw-tip to stinger continuously, like a living Jacob's ladder. Its stinger crackles with a condensed charge powerful enough to leave a six-meter circle of scorched earth when released. The ancient texts of Bug Thicket's keepers describe Thunderstinger as the Thicket's Enforcer: the last word spoken before silence falls.
stages.note: A Thunderstinger releasing a full charge stings only once - the recovering pause takes exactly twenty-four hours, and every bug in the Thicket goes quiet.

stages.name: Sparkub
stages.bio: Sparkub is a round little blue fish that bobs through the dark waterways of Storm Spire with a single golden glowing orb floating above its head like a miniature lighthouse. A thin purple swirl drifts in its wake - barely poisonous at this stage, more like a gentle warning smell - and it blinks its wide eyes at every tunnel junction as if uncertain of its route.
